'For them, day and night' means for those who attend in this way with the four requisites, their merit always increases day and night, both by way of giving and by way of recollection. 'And he goes to a heavenly place' means such a one, having done a good deed, goes to a heavenly place. In these four suttas, the householder's practice is taught. It is also suitable for stream-enterers and once-returners.

Puññābhisandavaggo paṭhamo.

The Chapter on the Overflow of Merit, the first.

(7) 2. Pattakammavaggo

(7) 2. The Chapter on Proper Action

1. Pattakammasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Pattakamma Sutta

61. Dutiyassa [V 2.0305][P 3.0098] paṭhame aniṭṭhapaṭikkhepena iṭṭhā. Mane kamanti pavisantīti kantā. Manaṃ appāyanti pavaḍḍhentīti manāpā. Dullabhāti paramadullabhā. Bhogāti bhuñjitabbā rūpādayo visayā. Sahadhammenāti dhammeneva saddhiṃ uppajjantu, mā dhammūpaghātaṃ katvā adhammenāti. Athavā sahadhammenāti sakāraṇena, tena tena senāpatiseṭṭhiṭṭhānādikāraṇena saddhiṃyeva uppajjantūti attho. Yasoti parivārasampatti. Saha [M 2.0313] ñātībhīti ñātakehi saddhiṃ. Saha upajjhāyehīti sukhadukkhesu upanijjhāyitabbattā upajjhāyasaṅkhātehi sandiṭṭhasambhattehi saddhiṃ.

61. In the first of the second, by the rejection of the undesirable, they are 'desirable' (iṭṭhā). They enter the mind, thus they are 'pleasing' (kantā). They augment and increase the mind, thus they are 'agreeable' (manāpā). 'Rare' means extremely rare. 'Possessions' means sense objects to be enjoyed, such as forms and so on. 'With the Dhamma' means may they arise together with the good Dhamma itself, not unrighteously by destroying the Dhamma. Alternatively, 'with the Dhamma' means with its cause; that is, may they arise together with this or that cause, such as the position of a general or a treasurer; this is the meaning. 'Fame' means the accomplishment of a retinue. 'With relatives' means together with kinsmen. 'With preceptors' means together with those called upajjhāya (observers) because they are to be closely observed in happiness and suffering, that is, with friends and companions.

Akiccaṃ karotīti akātabbaṃ karoti. Kiccaṃ aparādhetīti kattabbayuttakaṃ kiccaṃ akaronto taṃ aparādheti nāma. Dhaṃsatīti patati parihāyati. Abhijjhāvisamalobhanti abhijjhāsaṅkhātaṃ visamalobhaṃ. Pajahatīti nudati nīharati. Mahāpaññoti mahantapañño. Puthupaññoti puthulapañño. Āpātadasoti taṃ taṃ atthaṃ āpāteti tameva passati, sukhumampissa atthajātaṃ āpātaṃ āgacchatiyevāti attho.

'He does what is not a duty' means he does what should not be done. 'He fails in his duty' means not doing the task that should be done, he is said to fail in it. 'He is destroyed' means he falls, he declines. 'Covetousness and unrighteous greed' means the unrighteous greed called covetousness. 'He abandons' means he rejects, he expels. 'One of great wisdom' means having great wisdom. 'One of broad wisdom' means having broad wisdom. 'One who sees at a glance' means he sees this or that meaning as if it were standing in a clear place; for him, even a subtle class of meanings comes into appearance. This is the meaning.

Uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehīti [P 3.0099] uṭṭhānasaṅkhātena vīriyena adhigatehi. Bāhābalaparicitehīti bāhābalena paricitehi vaḍḍhitehi. Sedāvakkhittehīti avakkhittasedehi, sedaṃ muñcitvā vāyāmena payogena samadhigatehīti attho. Dhammikehīti dhammayuttehi. Dhammaladdhehīti dasakusalakammapathadhamme akopetvā laddhehi. Pattakammānīti yuttakammāni anucchavikakammāni. Sukhetīti sukhitaṃ karoti. Pīṇetīti pīṇitaṃ balasampannaṃ karoti. Ṭhānagataṃ hotīti kāraṇagataṃ hoti. Kiṃ pana tanti? Catūsu pattakammesu ekaṃ bhogehi kattabbakammaṃ bhogajātameva ṭhānagataṃ. Pattagatanti yuttappattaṭṭhānagataṃ. Āyatanaso paribhuttanti kāraṇeneva paribhuttaṃ bhogajātaṃ hoti.

'Attained by energy and effort' means attained by the energy known as exertion. 'Accumulated by arm-power' means accumulated and increased by arm-strength. 'With sweat pouring forth' means well attained by shedding sweat through effort and striving; this is the meaning. 'Righteous' means connected with the Dhamma. 'Righteously acquired' means acquired without violating the ten paths of wholesome action. 'Suitable deeds' means appropriate and fitting deeds. 'Makes happy' means makes one happy. 'Makes prosperous' means makes one replete and endowed with results. 'Comes to the proper place' means comes to the right cause. What then is that? Among the four suitable deeds, one is the action to be done with wealth; the wealth itself comes to the proper place. 'Gone to the proper place' means gone to the suitable and proper place. 'Used according to its purpose' means the wealth is used only according to its cause.

Pariyodhāya [V 2.0306] saṃvattatīti pidahitvā vattati. Yathā aggiādīhi uppannāsu āpadāsu, evaṃ ādittagehanibbāpanādīnaṃ atthāya dhanapariccāgaṃ katvā tāsaṃ āpadānaṃ maggaṃ pidahati nivāreti. Sotthiṃ attānaṃ karotīti nirupaddavaṃ khemaṃ attānaṃ karoti. Ñātibalinti ñātakānaṃ baliṃ. Atithibalinti āgantukānaṃ baliṃ. Pubbapetabalinti [P 3.0100] paralokagatānaṃ ñātakānaṃ baliṃ. Rājabalinti rañño kattabbayuttakaṃ rājabaliṃ. Devatābalinti devatānaṃ kattabbabaliṃ. Sabbametaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ yathānucchavikavasena dātabbadānassa adhivacanaṃ.

'Leads to obstruction' means it closes off and occurs. Just as when dangers arise from fire and the like, one makes a sacrifice of wealth to extinguish a burning house and so on, thereby closing off and preventing the path of those dangers. 'Makes oneself well' means makes oneself free from calamity and safe. 'The offering to relatives' means the offering to kin. 'The offering to guests' means the offering to visitors. 'The offering to the departed' means the offering for deceased relatives in the other world. 'The offering to the king' means the rightful offering to be made to the king. 'The offering to the deities' means the offering to be made to the deities. All these are terms for the giving of gifts appropriately according to each.

Khantisoracce niviṭṭhāti adhivāsanakkhantiyañca susīlatāya ca niviṭṭhā. Ekamattānaṃ damentīti ekaṃ attanova attabhāvaṃ indriyadamena damenti. Samentīti attano cittaṃ kilesavūpasamanena samenti. Parinibbāpentīti kilesaparinibbāneneva [M 2.0314] parinibbāpenti. Uddhaggikantiādīsu uparūparibhūmīsu phaladānavasena uddhamaggamassāti uddhaggikā. Saggassa hitāti tatrupapattijananato sovaggikā. Nibbattanibbattaṭṭhāne sukhova vipāko assāti sukhavipākā. Suṭṭhu aggānaṃ dibbavaṇṇādīnaṃ dasannaṃ visesānaṃ nibbattanato saggasaṃvattanikā, evarūpaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpetīti attho.

'Established in patience and good morality' means established in the patience of forbearance and in good morality. 'They tame a single self' means they tame their own single being through the taming of the senses. 'They calm' means they calm their own mind through the pacification of defilements. 'They bring to final cessation' means they bring to final cessation only through the extinguishing of defilements. Regarding 'leading upwards,' and so on: it is called `uddhaggikā` (leading upwards) because for this gift there is a supreme result in the higher and higher planes by the power of its fruition. It is `sovaggikā` (conducive to heaven) because it is for the welfare of heaven, generating rebirth there. It is `sukhavipākā` (resulting in happiness) because its result is only happiness in whatever place of rebirth. It is `saggasaṃvattanikā` (leading to heaven) because it produces the ten supreme special qualities, such as divine beauty and so forth. The meaning is that one establishes such a gift.

Ariyadhamme ṭhitoti pañcasīladhamme patiṭṭhito. Pecca sagge pamodatīti paralokaṃ gantvā yattha sagge paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhāti, tattha modati. Sotāpannasakadāgāmino vā hontu anāgāmī vā, sabbesaṃ ayaṃ paṭipadā labbhatevāti.

'Established in the noble Dhamma' means established in the five precepts. 'After death, one rejoices in heaven' means after passing to the other world, one rejoices in the heaven where rebirth is taken. Whether they are stream-enterers, once-returners, or non-returners, this practice is certainly attainable by all.

2. Ānaṇyasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Discourse on Debtlessness

62. Dutiye [P 3.0101] adhigamanīyānīti pattabbāni. Kāmabhogināti vatthukāme ca kilesakāme ca paribhuñjantena. Atthisukhādīsu atthīti uppajjanakasukhaṃ atthisukhaṃ nāma. Bhoge paribhuñjantassa uppajjanakasukhaṃ bhogasukhaṃ nāma. Anaṇosmīti uppajjanakasukhaṃ ānaṇyasukhaṃ nāma. Niddoso anavajjosmīti uppajjanakasukhaṃ anavajjasukhaṃ nāma.

62. In the second discourse, `adhigamanīyāni` means 'to be attained.' `Kāmabhoginā` means by one who enjoys both sensual objects and sensual defilements. Among 'the happiness of having,' and so on: the happiness that arises from the thought, 'I have wealth,' is called the happiness of having. The happiness that arises for one enjoying possessions is called the happiness of enjoyment. The happiness that arises from the thought, 'I am debtless,' is called the happiness of debtlessness. The happiness that arises from the thought, 'I am faultless and blameless,' is called the happiness of blamelessness.

Bhuñjanti bhuñjamāno. Paññā vipassatīti paññāya vipassati. Ubho bhāgeti dve koṭṭhāse, heṭṭhimāni tīṇi ekaṃ koṭṭhāsaṃ, anavajjasukhaṃ ekaṃ koṭṭhāsanti evaṃ paññāya passamāno [V 2.0307] dve koṭṭhāse jānātīti attho. Anavajjasukhassetanti etaṃ tividhampi sukhaṃ anavajjasukhassa soḷasiṃ kalaṃ nāgghatīti.

`Bhuñjaṃ` means 'while enjoying.' `Paññā vipassati` means one sees with wisdom. `Ubho bhāge` means two parts: the lower three happinesses are one part, and the happiness of blamelessness is one part. Thus, seeing with wisdom, one knows the two parts—this is the meaning. `Anavajjasukhassetaṃ` means that this threefold happiness is not worth a sixteenth part of the happiness of blamelessness.

3. Brahmasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Brahma Discourse

63. Tatiyaṃ tikanipāte vaṇṇitameva. Sapubbadevatānīti padamattameva ettha visesoti. Catutthe sabbaṃ uttānatthameva.

63. The third sutta has already been explained in the Tikanipāta. Here, only the term `sapubbadevatāni` is the distinction. In the fourth, everything has an obvious meaning.

5. Rūpasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Discourse on Form

65. Pañcame rūpe pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasanno rūpappamāṇo nāma. Rūpappasannoti tasseva atthavacanaṃ. Ghose pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasanno ghosappamāṇo [M 2.0315] nāma. Cīvaralūkhapattalūkhesu pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasanno lūkhappamāṇo nāma. Dhamme pamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasanno dhammappamāṇo nāma. Itarāni tesaṃyeva atthavacanāni. Sabbasatte [P 3.0102] ca tayo koṭṭhāse katvā dve koṭṭhāsā rūpappamāṇā, eko na rūpappamāṇo. Pañca koṭṭhāse katvā cattāro koṭṭhāsā ghosappamāṇā, eko na ghosappamāṇo. Dasa koṭṭhāse katvā nava koṭṭhāsā lūkhappamāṇā, eko na lūkhappamāṇo. Satasahassaṃ koṭṭhāse katvā pana eko koṭṭhāsova dhammappamāṇo, sesā na dhammappamāṇāti veditabbā.

65. In the fifth sutta, a person who is pleased, having taken form as the measure, is called 'one who measures by form' (`rūpappamāṇa`). `Rūpappasanna` is a term expressing that very meaning. A person who is pleased, having taken praise as the measure, is called 'one who measures by praise' (`ghosappamāṇa`). A person who is pleased, having taken the coarseness of robes and the coarseness of the bowl as the measure, is called 'one who measures by coarseness' (`lūkhappamāṇa`). A person who is pleased, having taken the Dhamma as the measure, is called 'one who measures by the Dhamma' (`dhammappamāṇa`). The other terms are expressions of the meaning of these very terms. Furthermore, having divided all beings into three parts, two parts measure by form, and one does not measure by form. Having divided them into five parts, four parts measure by praise, and one does not measure by praise. Having divided them into ten parts, nine parts measure by coarseness, and one does not measure by coarseness. However, having divided them into one hundred thousand parts, only one part measures by the Dhamma; it should be known that the rest do not measure by the Dhamma.

Rūpe pamāṇiṃsūti ye rūpaṃ disvā pasannā, te rūpe pamāṇiṃsu nāma, pasīdiṃsūti attho. Ghosena anvagūti ghosena anugatā, ghosappamāṇaṃ gahetvā pasannāti attho. Chandarāgavasūpetāti chandassa ca rāgassa ca vasaṃ upetā. Ajjhattañca na jānātīti niyakajjhatte tassa guṇaṃ na jānāti. Bahiddhā ca na passatīti bahiddhāpissa paṭipattiṃ na passati. Samantāvaraṇoti samantato āvārito, samantā vā āvaraṇamassāti samantāvaraṇo. Ghosena vuyhatīti ghosena niyati, na guṇena. Ajjhattañca na jānāti, bahiddhā ca vipassatīti niyakajjhatte guṇaṃ na jānāti, bahiddhā panassa paṭipattiṃ passati. Bahiddhā phaladassāvīti tassa parehi kataṃ bahiddhā sakkāraphalaṃ passanto. Vinīvaraṇadassāvīti vivaṭadassāvī. Na so ghosena vuyhatīti so ghosena na nīyati.

'Rūpe pamāṇiṃsu' means: those beings who are pleased upon seeing a form, they are called 'those who measured by form'; the meaning is 'they were pleased.' 'Ghosena anvagū' means: they followed after praise; the meaning is 'they were pleased, having taken praise as the measure.' 'Chandarāgavasūpetā' means: they have come under the power of desire and lust. 'Ajjhattañca na jānāti' means: one does not know that person's internal virtue. 'Bahiddhā ca na passati' means: one does not see that person's practice externally either. 'Samantāvaraṇo' means: obstructed from all around, or `samantāvaraṇo` is one for whom there is an obstruction all around. 'Ghosena vuyhati' means: one is led by praise, not by virtue. 'Ajjhattañca na jānāti, bahiddhā ca vipassati' means: one does not know the internal virtue, but one sees that person's practice externally. 'Bahiddhā phaladassāvī' means: seeing the fruit of honor done to that person by others externally. 'Vinīvaraṇadassāvī' means: one who sees the unobscured. 'Na so ghosena vuyhati' means: that person is not led by praise.

6. Sarāgasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Discourse on Lust

66. Chaṭṭhe [V 2.0308] mohajaṃ cāpaviddasūti mohajaṃ cāpi aviddasū apaṇḍitā. Savighātanti [P 3.0103] sadukkhaṃ. Dukhudrayanti āyatiñca dukkhavaḍḍhidāyakaṃ. Acakkhukāti paññācakkhurahitā. Yathā dhammā tathā santāti yathā rāgādayo dhammā ṭhitā, tathā sabhāvāva hutvā. Na tassevanti maññareti mayaṃ evaṃsantā evaṃsabhāvāti tassa na maññare, na maññantīti attho. Imasmiṃ suttepi gāthāsupi vaṭṭameva kathitaṃ.

66. In the sixth sutta, `mohajaṃ cāpaviddasūti`: the unwise, the foolish, also [commit deeds] born of delusion. `Savighātanti`: with suffering. `Dukhudrayanti`: leading to an increase of suffering also in the future. `Acakkhukāti`: devoid of the eye of wisdom. `Yathā dhammā tathā santāti`: just as phenomena such as greed exist, so they are, having that very nature. `Na tassevanti maññareti`: they do not conceive of that nature of theirs thus, 'We are thus, of such a nature'; the meaning is 'they do not conceive.' In this sutta and also in the verses, only the round of existence is taught.

7. Ahirājasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Discourse on Serpent Kings

67. Sattame [M 2.0316] imāni cattāri ahirājakulānīti idaṃ daṭṭhavisāneva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ye hi keci daṭṭhavisā, sabbete imesaṃ catunnaṃ ahirājakulānaṃ abbhantaragatāva honti. Attaguttiyāti attano guttatthāya. Attarakkhāyāti attano rakkhaṇatthāya. Attaparittāyāti attano parittāṇatthāya. Parittaṃ nāma anujānāmīti attho.

67. In the seventh sutta, this statement, 'these four royal families of serpents,' was spoken referring only to those with venom in their bite. For indeed, whatever serpents have venom in their bite, all of them are included within these four royal serpent families. `Attaguttiyāti`: for the purpose of protecting oneself. `Attarakkhāyāti`: for the purpose of guarding oneself. `Attaparittāyāti`: for the purpose of one's own safeguard. The meaning is: 'I permit a safeguard (paritta).'

Idāni yathā taṃ parittaṃ kātabbaṃ, taṃ dassento virūpakkhehi metiādimāha. Tattha virūpakkhehīti virūpakkhanāgakulehi. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Apādakehīti apādakasattehi. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Sabbe sattāti ito pubbe ettakena ṭhānena odissakamettaṃ kathetvā idāni anodissakamettaṃ kathetuṃ idamāraddhaṃ. Tattha sattā pāṇā bhūtāti sabbānetāni puggalavevacanāneva. Bhadrāni passantūti bhadrāni ārammaṇāni passantu. Mā kañci pāpamāgamāti kañci sattaṃ pāpakaṃ lāmakaṃ mā āgacchatu. Appamāṇo buddhoti ettha buddhoti buddhaguṇā veditabbā. Te hi appamāṇā nāma. Sesapadadvayepi [P 3.0104] eseva nayo. Pamāṇavantānīti guṇappamāṇena yuttāni. Uṇṇanābhīti lomasanābhiko makkaṭako. Sarabūti gharagolikā. Katā me rakkhā, katā me parittāti mayā ettakassa janassa rakkhā ca parittāṇañca kataṃ. Paṭikkamantu bhūtānīti sabbepi me kataparittāṇā sattā apagacchantu, mā maṃ viheṭhayiṃsūti attho.

Now, showing the manner in which that safeguard (paritta) is to be made, he spoke the words beginning with 'virūpakkhehi me...'. Therein, 'virūpakkhehi' means with the Virūpakkha nāga clan. In the remaining terms also, this is the method. 'Apādakehi' means with footless beings. In the remaining terms also, this is the method. Regarding the words 'Sabbe sattā': previously, having taught specified loving-kindness with this much of a passage, this was now begun by the Blessed One in order to teach unspecified loving-kindness. Therein, 'sattā', 'pāṇā', and 'bhūtā'—all these terms are indeed synonyms for an individual. 'Bhadrāni passantu' means may they see auspicious objects. 'Mā kañci pāpamāgamā' means may no evil, base thing come to any being. 'Appamāṇo buddho'—herein, by 'buddho' the virtues of the Buddha are to be understood. For they are indeed immeasurable. In the remaining two terms also, this is the method. 'Pamāṇavantāni' means endowed with a measure of virtues. 'Uṇṇanābhi' is a spider. 'Sarabū' is a house gecko. 'Katā me rakkhā, katā me parittā' means: by me, for this group of people, protection and a safeguard have been made. 'Paṭikkamantu bhūtāni' means: All safeguards have been made by me; may the beings depart. May they not harm me. This is the meaning.

8. Devadattasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Devadatta Discourse

68. Aṭṭhame [V 2.0309] acirapakkante devadatteti saṅghaṃ bhinditvā nacirapakkante. Parābhavāyāti avaḍḍhiyā vināsāya. Assatarīti vaḷavāya kucchismiṃ gadrabhassa jātā. Attavadhāya gabbhaṃ gaṇhātīti taṃ assena saddhiṃ sampayojenti, sā gabbhaṃ gaṇhitvā kāle sampatte vijāyituṃ nasakkontī pādehi bhūmiṃ paharantī tiṭṭhati. Athassā cattāro pāde catūsu khāṇūsu bandhitvā kucchiṃ phāletvā potakaṃ nīharanti. Sā tattheva marati. Tenetaṃ vuttaṃ.

68. In the eighth [discourse], ‘not long after Devadatta had departed’ means not long after he had departed, having caused a schism in the Saṅgha. ‘For ruin’ means for decline and destruction. ‘A mule’ means one born of a male donkey in the womb of a mare. ‘She conceives for her own destruction’ means: they pair her with a male donkey; having conceived, when the time comes, she is unable to give birth and stands striking the ground with her hooves. Then, tying her four legs to four posts, they cut open her belly and take out the young one. She dies right there. Therefore, this was said by the Blessed One.

9. Padhānasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Discourse on Exertion

69. Navame [M 2.0317] kilesānaṃ saṃvaratthāya pavesanadvāraṃ pidahanatthāya padhānaṃ saṃvarappadhānaṃ, pajahanatthāya padhānaṃ pahānappadhānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ brūhanatthāya vaḍḍhanatthāya padhānaṃ bhāvanāppadhānaṃ, tesaṃyeva anurakkhaṇatthāya padhānaṃ anurakkhaṇāppadhānaṃ.

69. In the ninth [discourse], the effort for the sake of guarding against the defilements, for the sake of closing the door of entry, is the effort of restraint (saṃvarappadhāna); the effort for the sake of abandoning [defilements] is the effort of abandoning (pahānappadhāna); the effort for the sake of increasing and developing wholesome qualities is the effort of development (bhāvanāppadhāna); and the effort for the sake of preserving those very [wholesome qualities] is the effort of preservation (anurakkhaṇāppadhāna).

10. Adhammikasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Adhammika Sutta

70. Dasame [P 3.0105] adhammikā hontīti porāṇakarājūhi ṭhapitaṃ dasabhāgabaliñceva aparādhānurūpañca daṇḍaṃ aggahetvā atirekabalino ceva atirekadaṇḍassa ca gahaṇena adhammikā. Rājāyuttāti rañño janapadesu kiccasaṃvidhāyakā āyuttakapurisā. Brāhmaṇagahapatikāti antonagaravāsino brāhmaṇagahapatayo. Negamajānapadāti nigamavāsino ceva janapadavāsino ca. Visamanti visamā hutvā, asamayena vāyantīti attho. Visamāti na samā, atithaddhā vā atimudukā vāti attho. Apañjasāti maggato apagatā, ummaggagāmino hutvā vāyantīti attho. Devatā parikupitā bhavantīti vātesu hi visamesu apañjasesu vāyantesu rukkhā bhijjanti, vimānāni bhijjanti. Tasmā devatā parikupitā bhavanti, tā devassa sammā vassituṃ na denti. Tena vuttaṃ devo na sammā dhāraṃ anuppavecchatīti. Visamapākāni sassāni bhavantīti ekasmiṃ ṭhāne gabbhīni honti, ekasmiṃ sañjātakhīrāni, ekaṃ ṭhānaṃ paccatīti evaṃ visamaṃ pākāni sassāni bhavanti.

70. In the tenth [discourse], ‘they are unrighteous’ means that, not taking the tax of a tenth part and the fines established by ancient kings in accordance with the offense, they are unrighteous by taking excessive taxes and excessive fines. ‘Appointed by the king’ refers to officials assigned by the king to manage affairs in the provinces. ‘Brahmins and householders’ means brahmins and householders living within the city. ‘Townsfolk and countryfolk’ refers to those living in towns and those living in the countryside. 'Visamaṃ' means: having become uneven, they blow at the wrong time. ‘Uneven’ means not uniform, that is, either too harsh or too soft. ‘Off-course’ means having deviated from the path, that is, they blow having become goers on a non-path. ‘The deities are displeased’ means that when winds blow unevenly and off-course, trees break and celestial mansions are destroyed. Therefore, the deities are displeased and do not allow the god to rain properly. Hence it is said, ‘the god does not send down a proper shower.’ ‘Crops ripen unevenly’ means in one place they are in the ear, in another they are at the milky stage, in another they are ripe—thus crops ripen unevenly.

Samaṃ [V 2.0310] nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni parivattantīti yathā kattikapuṇṇamā kattikanakkhattameva labhati, migasirapuṇṇamā migasiranakkhattamevāti evaṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ [P 3.0106] māse sā sā puṇṇamā taṃ taṃ nakkhattameva labhati, tathā sammā parivattanti. Samaṃ vātā vāyantīti avisamā hutvā samayasmiṃyeva vāyanti, cha māse uttarā vātā, cha māsedakkhiṇāti evaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ janapadānaṃ anurūpe samaye vāyanti. Samāti samappavattino nātithaddhā nātimudū. Pañjasāti maggappaṭipannā, maggeneva vāyanti, no amaggenāti attho.

‘The constellations, star-like in form, revolve evenly’ means that, just as the full moon in Kattika occurs in the Kattika constellation, and the full moon in Migasira occurs in the Migasira constellation—so in each month, each full moon occurs in its proper constellation; in this way they revolve harmoniously. ‘The winds blow evenly’ means they blow at the right time without being uneven—for six months northern winds, for six months southern winds—thus they blow in due season suitable for each region. ‘Even’ means proceeding uniformly, neither too stiff nor too mild. ‘Directed’ means proceeding on the path, that is, they blow only on the path, not off course.

Jimhaṃ [M 2.0318] gacchatīti kuṭilaṃ gacchati, atitthaṃ gaṇhāti. Nette jimhaṃ gate satīti nayatīti nettā. Tasmiṃ nette jimhaṃ gate kuṭilaṃ gantvā atitthaṃ gaṇhante itarāpi atitthameva gaṇhantīti attho. Netetipi pāṭho. Dukkhaṃ setīti dukkhaṃ sayati, dukkhitaṃ hotīti attho.

‘He goes crooked’ means he goes deviously, taking a non-ford. ‘When the leader goes crooked’ means: because it leads, it is called a leader. When that leader goes crooked, going deviously and taking a non-ford, the others also take only the non-ford; this is the meaning. ‘Neteti’ is also a reading. ‘He lies down in suffering’ means he lies down in suffering, that is, he is afflicted; this is the meaning.

Pattakammavaggo dutiyo.

The Chapter on Suitable Action, the Second.

(8) 3. Apaṇṇakavaggo

(8) 3. The Infallible Chapter

1. Padhānasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Discourse on Exertion

71. Tatiyavaggassa [V 2.0311] paṭhame apaṇṇakappaṭipadanti aviraddhappaṭipadaṃ. Yoni cassa āraddhā hotīti kāraṇañcassa paripuṇṇaṃ hoti. Āsavānaṃ khayāyāti arahattatthāya. Dutiyaṃ uttānameva.

71. In the first [discourse] of the third chapter, ‘infallible practice’ means unwavering practice. ‘And the source for it has been undertaken’ means its cause is fully complete. ‘For the destruction of the taints’ means for the sake of arahantship. The second [discourse] is self-evident.

3. Sappurisasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Discourse on the Good Person

73. Tatiye avaṇṇoti aguṇo. Pātu [P 3.0107] karotīti katheti, pākaṭaṃ karoti. Pañhābhinītoti pañhatthāya abhinīto. Ahāpetvā alambitvāti aparihīnaṃ alambitaṃ katvā. Ettha ca asappuriso pāpicchatāya attano avaṇṇaṃ chādeti, sappuriso lajjitāya attano vaṇṇaṃ. Idāni yasmā asappuriso hirottapparahito saṃvāsena avajānāti, sappuriso pana hirottappasamannāgato saṃvāsenāpi nāvajānāti. Tasmā asappurisabhāvasādhakaṃ adhunāgatavadhukopammaṃ dassetuṃ seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vadhukātiādimāha. Tattha vadhukāti suṇisā. Tibbanti bahalaṃ. Sesamettha uttānatthamevāti.

73. In the third discourse, ‘disgrace’ means a bad quality. ‘Makes known’ means declares, makes evident. ‘Brought for questioning’ means brought forth for the sake of a question. ‘Without diminishing, without causing to fade’ means having made it undiminished and unblemished. And here, an unrighteous person, due to evil desires, conceals his own disgrace, while a righteous person, due to conscientiousness, conceals his own virtue. Now, since an unrighteous person, being devoid of moral shame and moral dread, despises through association, but a righteous person, being endowed with moral shame and moral dread, does not despise even through association, therefore, to show the simile of the newly-arrived daughter-in-law which establishes the nature of an unrighteous person, he said, ‘Just as, bhikkhus, a daughter-in-law,’ and so forth. Therein, ‘daughter-in-law’ means a daughter-in-law. ‘Intense’ means dense. The rest here has an obvious meaning.

4-5. Aggasuttadvayavaṇṇanā

4-5. Commentary on the Two Agga Suttas

74-75. Catutthe sīlagganti aggappattaṃ uttamasīlaṃ. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Pañcame rūpagganti yaṃ rūpaṃ sammasitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, idaṃ rūpaggaṃ nāma. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Bhavagganti ettha pana yasmiṃ attabhāve ṭhito arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, etaṃ bhavaggaṃ nāmāti.

In the fourth sutta, 'culmination of virtue' (sīlagga) means virtue that has reached the highest state, supreme virtue. This is the method everywhere. In the fifth sutta, 'culmination of form' (rūpagga) means that form by comprehending which one attains Arahantship; this is called the culmination of form. The same method applies to the rest. But here, as for 'culmination of existence' (bhavagga), it means that individual existence in which, being established, one attains Arahantship; this is called the culmination of existence.

6. Kusinārasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Kusināra Sutta

76. Chaṭṭhe [V 2.0312][M 2.0319] upavattaneti pācīnagatāya sālapantiyā uttarena nivattitvā ṭhitāya vemajjhaṭṭhāne. Antarena yamakasālānanti dvinnaṃ sālarukkhānaṃ antare. Kaṅkhāti dveḷhakaṃ. Vimatīti vinicchituṃ asamatthatā. “Buddho nu kho na buddho nu kho, dhammo nu kho na dhammo nu kho, saṅgho nu kho na saṅgho nu kho, maggo nu kho na maggo nu kho, paṭipadā nu kho na paṭipadā nu kho”ti [P 3.0108] yassa saṃsayo uppajjeyya, taṃ vo vadāmi pucchatha, bhikkhaveti ayamettha saṅkhepattho. Satthugāravenapi na puccheyyāthāti “mayaṃ satthu santike pabbajimha, cattāro paccayāpi no satthu santakāva. Te mayaṃ ettakaṃ kālaṃ kaṅkhaṃ akatvā na arahāma ajja pacchime kāle kaṅkhaṃ kātu”nti sace evaṃ satthari gāravena na pucchatha. Sahāyakopi, bhikkhave, sahāyakassa ārocetūti tumhākaṃ yo yassa bhikkhussa sandiṭṭho sambhatto, so tassa ārocetu, ahaṃ ekassa bhikkhussa kathessāmi, tassa kathaṃ sutvā sabbe nikkaṅkhā bhavathāti dasseti. Evaṃ pasannoti evaṃ saddahāmi ahanti attho. Ñāṇamevāti nikkaṅkhabhāvapaccakkhakaraṇañāṇaṃyeva ettha tathāgatassa, na saddhāmattanti attho. Imesañhi, ānandāti imesaṃ antosāṇiyaṃ nisinnānaṃ pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ. Yo pacchimakoti yo guṇavasena pacchimako, ānandattheraṃyeva sandhāyāha.

76. In the sixth sutta: 'Upavattana' means the place situated midway in the row of sāl trees that stands, having turned northward from the row of sāl trees going to the east. 'Between the twin sāl trees' means between the two sāl trees. 'Doubt' (kaṅkhā) means indecision. 'Perplexity' (vimati) means the inability to decide. 'If for anyone a doubt should arise, such as: “Is he the Buddha or not? Is it the Dhamma or not? Is it the Saṅgha or not? Is it the path or not? Is it the practice or not?”—that I say to you, monks, ask.' This is the summary meaning here. 'Lest you not ask even out of respect for the Teacher' means: 'If, out of respect for the Teacher, you do not ask, thinking: “We went forth in the presence of the Teacher, and our four requisites are the Teacher's property. We, who have not had any doubt for so long, are not worthy to create doubt now at this last moment.”' 'Monks, let a companion inform a companion' shows this meaning: 'Whichever monk among you is an acquaintance or an intimate of another, let him inform that one. I will explain to one monk; having heard his explanation, may all of you become free from doubt.' 'Thus I have faith' means 'thus I believe.' 'Only knowledge' means: here, it is the Tathāgata's knowledge that directly realizes the state of being without doubt, not mere faith. 'Ānanda, among these' means among these five hundred monks seated within the curtained enclosure. 'Who is the last one' means the one who is last by way of virtue; this was said referring only to the Elder Ānanda.

7. Acinteyyasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Acinteyya Sutta

77. Sattame acinteyyānīti cintetuṃ ayuttāni. Na cintetabbānīti acinteyyattāyeva na cintetabbāni. Yāni cintentoti yāni kāraṇāni cintento. Ummādassāti ummattakabhāvassa. Vighātassāti dukkhassa. Buddhavisayoti buddhānaṃ visayo, sabbaññutaññāṇādīnaṃ buddhaguṇānaṃ pavatti ca ānubhāvo ca. Jhānavisayoti abhiññājhānavisayo. Kammavipākoti [P 3.0109] diṭṭhadhammavedanīyādīnaṃ kammānaṃ vipāko. Lokacintāti “kena nu kho candimasūriyā katā, kena mahāpathavī, kena mahāsamuddo, kena sattā uppāditā, kena pabbatā, kena ambatālanāḷikerādayo”ti evarūpā lokacintā.

77. In the seventh sutta, 'unthinkables' (acinteyyāni) means things that are improper to think about. 'Not to be thought about' (na cintetabbāni) means they should not be thought about precisely because they are unthinkable. 'One who thinks about them' (yāni cintento) means one who ponders these causes. 'Of madness' (ummādassa) means of the state of becoming mad. 'Of distress' (vighātassa) means of suffering. 'The domain of the Buddhas' (buddhavisayo) is the domain of the Buddhas—the occurrence and power of the Buddha’s qualities such as omniscience. 'The domain of jhāna' (jhānavisayo) is the domain of higher knowledge and jhāna. 'The result of kamma' (kammavipāko) is the fruit of kamma, such as kamma experienced in this very life. 'Speculation about the world' (lokacintā) means thoughts like, 'By whom were the moon and sun made? By whom was the great earth made? By whom was the great ocean made? By whom were beings produced? By whom were mountains made? By whom were trees like mangoes, palmyra palms, and coconuts made?'—such worldly speculations.

8. Dakkhiṇasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Dakkhiṇā Sutta

78. Aṭṭhame [V 2.0313][M 2.0320] dakkhiṇāvisuddhiyoti dānasaṅkhātāya dakkhiṇāya visujjhanakāraṇāni. Dāyakato visujjhatīti mahapphalabhāvena visujjhati, mahapphalā hotīti attho. Kalyāṇadhammoti sucidhammo. Pāpadhammoti lāmakadhammo. Dāyakato visujjhatīti ettha vessantaramahārājā kathetabbo. So hi jūjakabrāhmaṇassa dārake datvā mahāpathaviṃ kampesi. Paṭiggāhakato visujjhatīti ettha kalyāṇīnadīmukhadvāravāsī kevaṭṭo kathetabbo. So kira dīghasumattherassa tikkhattuṃ piṇḍapātaṃ datvā maraṇamañce nipanno “ayyassa maṃ dīghasumattherassa dinnapiṇḍapāto uddharatī”ti āha. Neva dāyakatoti ettha vaḍḍhamānavāsī luddako kathetabbo. So kira petadakkhiṇaṃ dento ekassa dussīlasseva tayo vāre adāsi. Tatiyavāre “amanusso dussīlo maṃ vilumpatī”ti viravi. Ekassa sīlavato bhikkhuno datvā pāpitakāleyevassa pāpuṇi. Dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato cāti ettha asadisadānaṃ kathetabbanti.

78. In the eighth sutta, 'purifications of offerings' (dakkhiṇāvisuddhiyo) means the causes for the purification of an offering, which is designated as a gift. 'Purified by the giver' (dāyakato visujjhati) means it is purified by way of being of great fruit; the meaning is that it becomes highly fruitful. 'Of good virtue' (kalyāṇadhammo) means of pure virtue. 'Of bad virtue' (pāpadhammo) means of base virtue. Regarding 'purified by the giver,' the story of King Vessantara should be told. For he, having given his children to the brahmin Jūjaka, caused the great earth to tremble. Regarding 'purified by the recipient' (paṭiggāhakato visujjhati), the story of the fisherman Kevaṭṭa, living at the mouth of the Kalyāṇī River, should be told. It is said that after offering alms-food three times to the Elder Dīghasuma, while lying on his deathbed, he said, 'The alms-food given to the noble Elder Dīghasuma saves me.' Regarding 'neither by the giver' (neva dāyakato), the story of the hunter from Vaḍḍhamāna should be told. It is said that while giving an offering for the deceased, he gave three times to just one immoral monk. On the third occasion, the deceased cried out, 'An immoral non-human is robbing me!' But when the hunter gave to a virtuous monk, the offering reached the deceased only when the merit was dedicated. Regarding 'purified both by the giver and by the recipient' (dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca), the story of the unequalled gift should be told.

9. Vaṇijjasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Vaṇijja Sutta

79. Navame [P 3.0110] tādisā vāti taṃsadisāva taṃsarikkhakāva. Chedagāminī hotīti chedaṃ gacchati. Yaṃ patthitaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ nassatīti attho. Na yathādhippāyā hotīti yathājjhāsayā na hoti. Parādhippāyā hotīti parajjhāsayā ajjhāsayato adhikataraphalā hoti. Samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vāti ettha samitapāpabāhitapāpatāhi samaṇabrāhmaṇatā veditabbā. Vadatu, bhante, paccayenāti, bhante, catubbidhena cīvarādinā paccayena vadeyyāsīti evaṃ pavāreti nimanteti. Yena pavāretīti paricchinditvā yattakena pavāreti. Taṃ na detīti taṃ sabbasova na deti. Na yathādhippāyaṃ detīti yathā tassa ajjhāsayo, evaṃ dātuṃ na sakkoti, hāpetvā appakaṃ deti. Yathādhippāyaṃ detīti yattakaṃ so icchati, tattakameva deti. Parādhippāyaṃ detīti appakaṃ pavāretvā avattharitvā bahuṃ deti.

79. In the ninth sutta, 'just like that' (tādisā) means just like that, similar to that. 'Leads to destruction' (chedagāminī hoti) means it goes to the destruction of capital and profit; the meaning is that all the capital and profit that is desired is destroyed. 'Not as intended' (na yathādhippāyā hoti) means it is not according to one's wish. 'Exceeding the intention' (parādhippāyā hoti) means it yields a result that is much greater than one's wish. Regarding 'an ascetic or a brahmin' (samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā), here the state of being an ascetic or a brahmin should be understood through the calming of evil and the dispelling of evil. 'May you speak, venerable sir, by means of the requisites' (vadatu, bhante, paccayena) means he invites or requests thus: 'Venerable sir, may you ask by means of the fourfold requisites such as robes.' 'With which he invites' (yena pavāreti) means having delimited, he invites with a certain amount. 'He does not give that' (taṃ na deti) means he does not give all of it. 'He does not give as intended' (na yathādhippāyaṃ deti) means he is unable to give according to the recipient's wish; having reduced it, he gives a small amount. 'He gives as intended' (yathādhippāyaṃ deti) means he gives exactly as much as the recipient wishes. 'He gives exceeding the intention' (parādhippāyaṃ deti) means having invited with a small amount, he gives a large amount, overwhelming it.

10. Kambojasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Kamboja Sutta

80. Dasame [M 2.0321] neva sabhāyaṃ nisīdatīti vinicchayakaraṇatthaṃ vinicchayasabhāyaṃ neva nisīdati[V 2.0314]. Na kammantaṃ payojetīti kasivaṇijjādimahākammantaṃ nappayojeti. Na kambojaṃ gacchatīti bhoge sambharaṇatthāya kambojaraṭṭhaṃ na gacchati. Desanāmattameva cetaṃ, yaṃ kiñci tiroraṭṭhaṃ na gacchatīti attho. Kodhanotiādīsu kodhanatāya kodhapariyuṭṭhito atthānatthaṃ na jānāti, issukitāya parasampattiṃ na sahati, maccharitāya [P 3.0111] dhanaṃ datvā kiccaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, nippaññatāya kiccaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ na sakkoti. Tasmā etāni sabhānisīdanādīni na karotīti.

80. In the tenth sutta, 'she does not sit in an assembly' means she does not sit in a judicial assembly for the purpose of making a judgment. 'She does not engage in work' means she does not undertake major work such as agriculture and trade. 'She does not go to Kamboja' means she does not go to the country of Kamboja for the purpose of accumulating wealth. This is merely an illustrative teaching; the meaning is that she does not go to any foreign country. Regarding 'angry' and so on: due to being angry, a woman overcome by anger does not know what is beneficial and what is not; due to being envious, she cannot bear the prosperity of others; due to stinginess, she is unable to get things done by giving wealth; due to being unwise, she is unable to manage affairs. Therefore, she does not do these things, such as sitting in an assembly.

Apaṇṇakavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter

(9) 4. Macalavaggo

(9) 4. The Macala Chapter

1-5. Pāṇātipātādisuttapañcakavaṇṇanā

1–5. Commentary on the Pentad of Suttas Beginning with the Killing of Living Beings

81-85. Catutthassa [V 2.0315] paṭhamādīni uttānatthāneva. Pañcame “nīce kule paccājāto”tiādikena tamena yuttoti tamo. Kāyaduccaritādīhi puna nirayatamūpagamanato tamaparāyaṇo. Iti ubhayenapi khandhatamova kathito hoti. “Aḍḍhe kule paccājāto”tiādikena jotinā yuttato joti, ālokabhūtoti vuttaṃ hoti. Kāyasucaritādīhi puna sagguppattijotibhāvūpagamanato jotiparāyaṇo. Iminā nayena itarepi dve veditabbā.

The first suttas and so on of the fourth chapter are clear in meaning. In the fifth, regarding the passage beginning with 'born in a low family,' because one is associated with that which is darkness (tamena), one is 'darkness' (tamo). Again, through bodily misconduct and so on, because of approaching the darkness of hell, one is 'destined for darkness' (tamaparāyaṇo). Thus, by both terms, it is the darkness of the aggregates that is spoken of. Regarding the passage beginning with 'born in a wealthy family,' because one is associated with light (jotinā), one is 'light' (joti); it is said that one has become luminous. Again, through bodily good conduct and so on, because of approaching the light-state of rebirth in the celestial realm, one is 'destined for light' (jotiparāyaṇo). In this way, the other two pairs should also be understood.

Venakuleti vilīvakārakule. Nesādakuleti migaluddakādīnaṃ kule. Rathakārakuleti cammakārakule. Pukkusakuleti pupphachaḍḍakakule. Kasiravuttiketi dukkhavuttike. Dubbaṇṇoti [P 3.0112] paṃsupisācako viya jhāmakhāṇuvaṇṇo. Duddasikoti vijātamātuyāpi amanāpadassano. Okoṭimakoti lakuṇḍako. Kāṇoti ekacchikāṇo vā ubhayacchikāṇo vā. Kuṇīti ekahatthakuṇī vā ubhayahatthakuṇī vā. Khañjoti ekapādakhañjo vā ubhayapādakhañjo vā. Pakkhahatoti hatapakkho pīṭhasappī[M 2.0322]. Padīpeyyassāti telakapallādino dīpaupakaraṇassa. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhaveti ettha eko puggalo bahiddhā ālokaṃ adisvā mātu kucchimhiyeva kālaṃ katvā apāyesu nibbattanto sakalampi kappaṃ saṃsarati. Sopi tamotamaparāyaṇova. So pana kuhakapuggalo bhaveyya. Kuhakassa hi evarūpā nipphatti hotīti vuttaṃ.

‘In a family of reed-workers’ (venakule) means in a family of basket-makers. ‘In a family of hunters’ (nesādakule) means in the family of hunters of wild animals and so on. ‘In a family of chariot-makers’ (rathakārakule) means in a family of leather-workers. ‘In a Pukkusa family’ (pukkusakule) means in a family of flower-refuse removers. ‘Of difficult livelihood’ (kasiravuttike) means having a miserable livelihood. ‘Of poor complexion’ (dubbaṇṇo) means having a complexion like a burnt stump, like a dust-goblin. ‘Difficult to look at’ (duddasiko) means having an appearance unpleasant even to the mother who gave birth to him. ‘Stunted’ (okoṭimako) means a dwarf. ‘Blind’ (kāṇo) means blind in one eye or in both eyes. ‘Crippled’ (kuṇī) means crippled in one hand or in both hands. ‘Lame’ (khañjo) means lame in one leg or in both legs. ‘Paralyzed’ (pakkhahato) means one whose lower body is afflicted, who moves about on a wheeled board. ‘For a lamp’ (padīpeyyassa) means for lamp equipment, such as an oil-lamp bowl. In the passage, ‘Thus, O bhikkhus,’ a certain person, not seeing the light outside, dies right in the mother’s womb and, being reborn in the woeful states, wanders for an entire eon. That person, too, is one of darkness, destined for darkness. That, however, might be a deceitful person. For it is said that such a destiny is for a deceitful one.

Ettha ca “nīce kule”tiādīhi āgamanavipatti ceva paccuppannapaccayavipatti ca dassitā. “Dalidde”tiādīhi pavattapaccayavipatti, “kasiravuttike”tiādīhi ājīvupāyavipatti, “dubbaṇṇo”tiādīhi attabhāvavipatti, “bahvābādho”tiādīhi dukkhakāraṇasamāyogo, “na lābhī”tiādīhi sukhakāraṇavipatti ceva upabhogavipatti ca, “kāyena duccarita”ntiādīhi tamaparāyaṇabhāvassa kāraṇasamāyogo, “kāyassa bhedā”tiādīhi samparāyikatamūpagamo. Sukkapakkho vuttapaṭipakkhanayena veditabbo.

Herein, 'in a low family,' etc., indicates both deficiency of origin and deficiency of present conditions. 'Poor,' etc., indicates deficiency of ongoing conditions; 'living with difficulty,' etc., deficiency of livelihood; 'ugly,' etc., deficiency of personal existence; 'afflicted with many illnesses,' etc., association with the cause of suffering; 'not obtaining,' etc., both deficiency in the cause of happiness and deficiency of enjoyment; 'bodily misconduct,' etc., association with the cause for a future state of darkness; 'upon the breakup of the body,' etc., the going to darkness in the next life. The bright side is to be understood in the opposite way to what has been stated.

6. Oṇatoṇatasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Oṇatoṇata Sutta

86. Chaṭṭhe [V 2.0316] oṇatoṇatoti idāni nīcako āyatimpi nīcako bhavissati. Oṇatuṇṇatoti idāni nīco āyatiṃ ucco bhavissati. Uṇṇatoṇatoti idāni ucco āyatiṃ nīco bhavissati. Uṇṇatuṇṇatoti [P 3.0113] idāni ucco āyatimpi ucco bhavissati. Vitthāro pana nesaṃ purimasuttanayeneva veditabbo.

86. In the sixth sutta, 'inferior to inferior' (oṇatoṇato) means one who is inferior now will be inferior in the future as well. 'Inferior to superior' (oṇatuṇṇato) means one who is inferior now will become superior in the future. 'Superior to inferior' (uṇṇatoṇato) means one who is superior now will become inferior in the future. 'Superior to superior' (uṇṇatuṇṇato) means one who is superior now will be superior in the future as well. The detailed explanation of these should be understood in the same way as in the previous sutta.

7. Puttasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Putta Sutta

87. Sattame samaṇamacaloti samaṇaacalo, makāro padasandhikaro, niccalasamaṇoti attho. Iminā sattavidhampi sekhaṃ dasseti. So hi sāsane mūlajātāya saddhāya patiṭṭhitattā acalo nāma. Samaṇapuṇḍarīkoti puṇḍarīkasadiso samaṇo. Puṇḍarīkaṃ nāma ūnasatapattaṃ saroruhaṃ. Iminā sukkhavipassakakhīṇāsavaṃ dasseti. So hi jhānābhiññānaṃ abhāvena aparipuṇṇaguṇattā samaṇapuṇḍarīko nāma hoti. Samaṇapadumoti padumasadiso samaṇo. Padumaṃ nāma paripuṇṇasatapattaṃ saroruhaṃ. Iminā ubhatobhāgavimuttaṃ khīṇāsavaṃ dasseti. So hi jhānābhiññānaṃ bhāvena paripuṇṇaguṇattā samaṇapadumo nāma hoti[M 2.0323]. Samaṇesu samaṇasukhumāloti sabbesupi etesu samaṇesu sukhumālasamaṇo muducittasarīro kāyikacetasikadukkharahito ekantasukhī. Etena attānañceva attasadise ca dasseti.

87. In the seventh, 'the steadfast ascetic' (samaṇamacalo) is samaṇa-acalo. The 'ma' is for euphonic conjunction; the meaning is 'an unwavering ascetic'. This indicates the seven kinds of learners. For he is called 'steadfast' because he is firmly established in the faith that has taken root in the Teaching. 'The white lotus ascetic' (samaṇapuṇḍarīko) is an ascetic like a white lotus. A puṇḍarīka is a lotus with fewer than a hundred petals. This signifies a dry-insight practitioner who has destroyed the taints. He is called a 'white lotus ascetic' because his qualities are incomplete due to the absence of meditative absorptions and higher knowledges. 'The red lotus ascetic' (samaṇapadumo) is an ascetic like a red lotus. A paduma is a lotus with a full hundred petals. This signifies one liberated in both ways, who has destroyed the taints. He is called a 'red lotus ascetic' because his qualities are complete due to the presence of meditative absorptions and higher knowledges. 'Among ascetics, the delicate ascetic' (samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo) is, among all these ascetics, the delicate ascetic with a gentle mind and body, free from physical and mental suffering, and utterly blissful. By this, he indicates both himself and those like him.

Evaṃ mātikaṃ nikkhipitvā idāni paṭipāṭiyā vibhajanto kathañca, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha sekhoti sattavidhopi sekho. Pāṭipadoti paṭipannako. Anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamāno viharatīti arahattaṃ patthayanto viharati. Muddhāvasittassāti muddhani avasittassa, katābhisekassāti attho. Ābhisekoti abhisekaṃ kātuṃ yutto. Anabhisittoti [P 3.0114] na tāva abhisitto. Macalappattoti rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa puttabhāvena ceva puttesu jeṭṭhakabhāvena ca na tāva abhisittabhāvena ca abhisekappattiatthāya acalappatto niccalapatto. Makāro nipātamattaṃ. Kāyena phusitvāti nāmakāyena phusitvā.

Having laid down the matrix in this way, now explaining in sequence, he says, “How, O monks?” and so on. Here, 'a learner' refers to a learner of seven kinds. 'Practicing' means one who has entered upon the path. 'Dwelling aspiring for the unsurpassed security from bondage' means dwelling aspiring for arahantship. 'One whose head is anointed' means one who has been anointed on the head, that is, whose consecration has been performed. 'Fit for consecration' means suitable to receive the consecration. 'Not yet consecrated' means not yet consecrated. 'One who has attained stability' means that, as the eldest son of a noble king whose head has been anointed, by virtue of being a son and being the eldest among sons, and because he has not yet been consecrated, he has attained the stability for consecration, an unshakeable, firm attainment. The letter 'm' is merely a particle. 'Touched by the body' means touched by the mental body.

Yācitova bahulaṃ cīvaraṃ paribhuñjatīti “idaṃ, bhante, paribhuñjathā”ti evaṃ dāyakehi yācamāneheva [V 2.0317] upanītaṃ cīvaraṃ bahuṃ paribhuñjati, kiñcideva ayācitaṃ, bākulatthero viya. Piṇḍapātaṃ khadiravanamagge sīvalitthero viya. Senāsanaṃ aṭṭhakanāgarasutte (ma. ni. 2.17 ādayo; a. ni. 11.16 ādayo) ānandatthero viya. Gilānapaccayaṃ pilindavacchathero viya. Tyassāti te assa. Manāpenevāti manaṃ allīyanakena. Samudācarantīti kattabbakiccāni karonti pavattanti vā. Upahāraṃ upaharantīti kāyikacetasikaupahāraṃ upaharanti upanīyanti. Sannipātikānīti tiṇṇampi sannipātena nibbattāni. Utupariṇāmajānīti utupariṇāmato atisītaatiuṇhaututo jātāni. Visamaparihārajānīti accāsanaatiṭṭhānādikā visamaparihārato jātāni. Opakkamikānīti vadhabandhanādiupakkamena nibbattāni. Kammavipākajānīti [P 3.0115] vināpi imehi kāraṇehi kevalaṃ pubbe katakammavipākavaseneva jātāni. Catunnaṃ jhānānanti ettha khīṇāsavānampi buddhānampi kiriyajjhānāneva adhippetāni. Sesaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

“He uses much robe-cloth only when requested” means that when donors say, “Venerable sir, please use this,” he uses much robe-cloth brought by donors only upon their request, and only a little that is unrequested, like the Elder Bākula. For almsfood, it is like the Elder Sīvali on the Khadiravana road. For lodging, it is like the Elder Ānanda in the Aṭṭhakanāgara Sutta. For medicinal requisites, it is like the Elder Pilindavaccha. ‘Tyassa’ is ‘te assa’. ‘Pleasingly’ means in a way that attracts the mind. ‘They attend upon him’ means they perform the duties that should be done, or they behave accordingly. ‘They offer service’ means they offer and present bodily and mental service. ‘Arising from a combination’ means produced by the coming together of the three humors. ‘Arising from a change of season’ means arising from a change in the weather—from a season of excessive cold or excessive heat. ‘Arising from uneven care’ means arising from improper activities like excessive sitting or standing. ‘Arising from assault’ means produced by attacks such as killing or imprisonment. ‘Arising from the result of kamma’ means arising solely by the power of the result of kamma done previously, even without these other causes. Regarding ‘of the four jhānas’—here, even for those with taints destroyed and for Buddhas, only functional jhānas are intended. The rest has a clear meaning.

8. Saṃyojanasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Saṃyojana Sutta

88. Aṭṭhame sāsane laddhappatiṭṭhattā sotāpannova samaṇamacaloti vutto, nātibahuguṇattā na bahupattaṃ viya saroruhaṃ sakadāgāmī [M 2.0324] samaṇapuṇḍarīkoti, tato bahutaraguṇattā satapattaṃ viya saroruhaṃ anāgāmī samaṇapadumoti, thaddhabhāvakarānaṃ kilesānaṃ sabbaso samucchinnattā mudubhāvappatto khīṇāsavo samaṇasukhumāloti.

88. In the eighth, because of having attained a firm footing in the Dispensation, the stream-enterer is called the steadfast ascetic. Not having an abundance of qualities, like a lotus with few petals, the once-returner is called the white-lotus ascetic. Having even more qualities than that, like a lotus with a hundred petals, the non-returner is called the red-lotus ascetic. Because the defilements that cause rigidity have been completely uprooted and he has attained a state of softness, the one with taints destroyed is called the delicate ascetic.

9. Sammādiṭṭhisuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta

89. Navame sammādiṭṭhikotiādīhi aṭṭhaṅgikamaggavasena paṭhamasutte viya satta sekhā gahitā. Dutiyavāre dasaṅgikamaggavasena vā arahattaphalañāṇaarahattaphalavimuttīhi saddhiṃ, aṭṭhaṅgikamaggavasena vā sukkhavipassakakhīṇāsavo kathito, tatiyavāre ubhatobhāgavimutto, catutthavāre tathāgato ca tathāgatasadisakhīṇāsavo cāti. Iti idaṃ suttaṃ paṭhamasutte kathitapuggalānaṃ vaseneva kathitaṃ, desanāmattameva panettha nānanti.

89. In the ninth, by ‘one of right view’ and so on, the seven learners are included by way of the eightfold path, as in the first discourse. In the second instance, either by way of the tenfold path, along with the knowledge of the fruition of arahantship and the liberation of the fruition of arahantship, or by way of the eightfold path, the dry-insight arahant is spoken of. In the third instance, the one liberated in both ways is spoken of. In the fourth instance, the Tathāgata and an arahant similar to the Tathāgata are spoken of. Thus, this discourse is taught by way of the same individuals as spoken of in the first discourse; only the method of teaching is different here.

10. Khandhasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Khandha Sutta

90. Dasame [V 2.0318] paṭhamavāre arahattatthāya payogaṃ anārabhitvā ṭhito pamādavihārī sekhapuggalo kathito. Dutiyavāre anuppāditajjhāno āraddhavipassako appamādavihārī sekhapuggalo kathito. Tatiyavāre āraddhavipassako appamādavihārī aṭṭhavimokkhalābhī sekhapuggalo kathito, catutthavāre paramasukhumālakhīṇāsavoti.

90. In the tenth, in the first instance, a learner dwelling in negligence, who stands without having initiated effort for arahantship, is described. In the second instance, a diligent learner who has not produced jhāna but has commenced insight is described. In the third instance, a diligent learner who has commenced insight and has attained the eight liberations is described. In the fourth instance, an extremely delicate one whose taints are destroyed is described.

Macalavaggo catuttho.

The Macala Chapter is the fourth.

(10) 5. Asuravaggo

(10) 5. The Asura Chapter

1. Asurasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Asura Sutta

91. Pañcamassa [V 2.0319][P 3.0116] paṭhame asuroti asurasadiso bībhaccho. Devoti devasadiso guṇavasena abhirūpo pāsādiko.

91. In the first of the fifth, 'asura' means repulsive, like an asura. 'Deva' means beautiful and admirable in terms of qualities, like a deva.

2. Paṭhamasamādhisuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the First Samādhi Sutta

92. Dutiye [M 2.0325] ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassāti niyakajjhatte appanācittasamādhissa. Adhipaññādhammavipassanāyāti saṅkhārapariggāhakavipassanāñāṇassa. Tañhi adhipaññāsaṅkhātañca, pañcakkhandhasaṅkhātesu ca dhammesu vipassanābhūtaṃ, tasmā “adhipaññādhammavipassanā”ti vuccatīti.

92. In the second, ‘of internal serenity of mind’ means of the concentration of absorption pertaining to one's own interior. ‘Of insight into phenomena through higher wisdom’ means of the insight-knowledge that comprehends formations. For that knowledge is reckoned as higher wisdom, and it is insight into the phenomena known as the five aggregates; therefore it is called ‘insight into phenomena through higher wisdom’.

3. Dutiyasamādhisuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Second Samādhi Sutta

93. Tatiye yogo karaṇīyoti yuttappayuttatā kattabbā. Chandoti kattukamyatāchando. Vāyāmoti payogo. Ussāhoti tato adhimattataraṃ vīriyaṃ. Ussoḷhīti paṅkalaggasakaṭauddharaṇasadisaṃ mahāvīriyaṃ. Appaṭivānīti anivattanatā.

93. In the third [sutta], 'effort is to be made' means the state of being engaged and applied is to be undertaken. 'Zeal' is the desire to act. 'Exertion' is application. 'Striving' is energy even more excessive than that. 'Persistence' is great energy, like that for extricating a cart stuck in the mud. 'Unyielding' means not turning back.

4. Tatiyasamādhisuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Third Samādhi Sutta

94. Catutthe evaṃ kho, āvuso, saṅkhārā daṭṭhabbātiādīsu, āvuso, saṅkhārā nāma aniccato daṭṭhabbā, aniccato sammasitabbā, aniccato passitabbā. Tathā dukkhato, anattatoti evaṃ attho daṭṭhabbo. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, cittaṃ saṇṭhapetabbantiādīsupi paṭhamajjhānavasena, āvuso, cittaṃ saṇṭhapetabbaṃ paṭhamajjhānavasena sannisādetabbaṃ, paṭhamajjhānavasena [V 2.0320] ekodi kātabbaṃ, paṭhamajjhānavasena samādahitabbaṃ. Tathā dutiyajjhānādivasenāti evaṃ attho daṭṭhabbo. Imesu tīsupi suttesu samathavipassanā lokiyalokuttarāva kathitā.

94. In the fourth [sutta], regarding 'Thus, friends, formations should be seen,' and so on: formations, friends, should be seen, contemplated, and perceived as impermanent. Similarly, the meaning should be understood as 'suffering' and 'not-self.' Regarding 'Thus, friends, the mind should be steadied,' and so on: the mind, friends, should be steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated by means of the first jhāna. Likewise, the meaning should be understood as by means of the second jhāna, and so on. In these three suttas, both mundane and supramundane serenity and insight are taught.

5. Chavālātasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Chavālāta Sutta

95. Pañcame chavālātanti susāne alātaṃ. Majjhe [P 3.0117] gūthagatanti majjhaṭṭhāne gūthamakkhitaṃ. Neva gāme kaṭṭhatthaṃ pharatīti kūṭagopānasithambhasopānādīnaṃ atthāya anupaneyyatāya gāme na kaṭṭhatthaṃ sādheti, khettakuṭipādaṃ vā mañcapādaṃ vā kātuṃ anupaneyyatāya na araññe kaṭṭhatthaṃ sādheti. Dvīsu koṭīsu gayhamānaṃ hatthaṃ ḍahati, majjhe gayhamānaṃ gūthena makkheti. Tathūpamanti taṃsarikkhakaṃ. Abhikkantataroti sundarataro. Paṇītataroti uttamataro. Gavā khīranti gāvito khīraṃ. Khīramhā dadhītiādīsu paraṃ paraṃ purimato purimato aggaṃ, sappimaṇḍo pana tesu sabbesupi aggameva[M 2.0326]. Aggotiādīsu guṇehi aggo ceva seṭṭho ca pamukho ca uttamo ca pavaro cāti veditabbo. Chavālātūpamāya na dussīlo puggalo kathito, appassuto pana vissaṭṭhakammanto goṇasadiso puggalo kathitoti veditabbo. Chaṭṭhe sabbaṃ uttānatthameva.

95. In the fifth [sutta], 'chavālāta' means a firebrand from a charnel ground. 'Smeared with dung in the middle' means smeared with dung in its middle part. 'It does not serve the purpose of wood in the village' means that because it is unsuitable to be brought for the purpose of ridgepoles, roof beams, pillars, stairs, and so on, it does not fulfill the purpose of wood in the village; and because it is unsuitable for making the leg of a field-hut or the leg of a bed, it does not fulfill the purpose of wood in the forest. When grasped at the two ends, it burns the hand; when grasped in the middle, it smears one with dung. 'Of such a likeness' means similar to that. 'More excellent' means more beautiful. 'More sublime' means more superior. 'Milk from a cow' means milk from a cow. Regarding 'from milk, curds,' and so on, each subsequent product is superior to the one preceding it, but the cream of ghee is the most superior of them all. Regarding 'foremost,' and so on, it should be understood as foremost, best, chief, supreme, and excellent in its qualities. By the simile of the firebrand from a charnel ground, an immoral person is not spoken of; rather, an unlearned person of abandoned conduct, similar to an ox, is spoken of—this is to be understood. In the sixth [sutta], everything is of clear meaning.

7. Khippanisantisuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Khippanisanti Sutta

97. Sattame khippanisantīti khippanisāmano sīghaṃ jānituṃ samattho. Sutānañca dhammānanti sutappaguṇānaṃ tantidhammānaṃ. Atthūpaparikkhīti atthaṃ upaparikkhako. Atthamaññāya dhammamaññāyāti aṭṭhakathañca pāḷiñca jānitvā. Dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hotīti navalokuttaradhammānaṃ [P 3.0118] anurūpadhammabhūtaṃ sasīlakaṃ pubbabhāgappaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno hoti. No ca kalyāṇavācoti na sundaravacano. Na kalyāṇavākkaraṇoti na sundaravacanaghoso hoti. Poriyātiādīhi saddhiṃ no-kāro yojetabboyeva. Guṇaparipuṇṇāya apalibuddhāya adosāya agaḷitapadabyañjanāya atthaṃ viññāpetuṃ samatthāya vācāya samannāgato na hotīti attho. Iminā upāyena sabbattha attho veditabbo.

97. In the seventh [sutta], 'one who is quick to comprehend' means one who is quick to discern, able to understand swiftly. 'Of the teachings heard' means of the well-practiced teachings of the canon. 'An examiner of the meaning' means one who investigates the meaning. 'Having understood the meaning and having understood the teaching' means having known both the commentary and the Pāli text. 'One who practices in accordance with the Dhamma' means one practices the preliminary path, which is endowed with virtue and is the appropriate practice for the nine supramundane Dhammas. 'And is not one of good speech' means one does not have beautiful speech. 'Not one of good utterance' means one does not have a beautifully sounding voice. The negative particle 'no' is to be connected with 'porī' (eloquent), and so on. The meaning is that one is not endowed with speech that is complete in its qualities, unobstructed, faultless, with unslurred words and syllables, and capable of making the meaning known. In this way, the meaning should be understood everywhere.

8. Attahitasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Attahita Sutta

98-99. Aṭṭhamaṃ [V 2.0321] puggalajjhāsayavasenāpi dasabalassa desanāñāṇavilāsenāpi kathitaṃ, navamaṃ pañcaveravasena.

The eighth [sutta] was taught according to the disposition of individuals and also through the graceful display of the Ten-Powered One’s knowledge of teaching. The ninth was taught by way of the five kinds of enmity.

10. Potaliyasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Potaliya Sutta

100. Dasame kālenāti yuttappattakālena. Khamatīti ruccati. Yadidaṃ tattha tattha kālaññutāti yā esā tattha tattha kālaṃ jānanā. Taṃ taṃ kālaṃ ñatvā hi avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇakathanaṃ vaṇṇārahassa ca vaṇṇakathanaṃ paṇḍitānaṃ pakatīti dasseti.

100. In the tenth [sutta], 'at the right time' means at a suitable and appropriate time. 'It is approved of' means it is pleasing. 'That is, the knowledge of the right time in each case' means that which is the knowing of the time in each case. This shows that, having known the particular time, to speak dispraise of one worthy of dispraise and to speak praise of one worthy of praise is the nature of the wise.

Asuravaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter: The Asuras.

Dutiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Fifty is Concluded.

3. Tatiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ

3. The Third Fifty

(11) 1. Valāhakavaggo

(11) 1. The Chapter on Clouds

1-2. Valāhakasuttadvayavaṇṇanā

1–2. Commentary on the Two Suttas about Clouds

101-2. Tatiyapaṇṇāsakassa [V 2.0322][M 2.0327][P 3.0119] paṭhame valāhakāti meghā. Bhāsitā hoti no kattāti “idañcidañca karissāmī”ti kevalaṃ bhāsatiyeva, na karoti. Kattā hoti no bhāsitāti akathetvāva “idañcidañca mayā kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti kattā hoti. Evaṃ sabbattha attho veditabbo. Dutiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

In the first [sutta] of the Third Fifty, 'clouds' means rain clouds. 'One who speaks but does not act' means one who only says, “I will do this and that,” but does not do it. 'One who acts but does not speak' means one who acts without having spoken, thinking, “It is right that this and that be done by me.” In this way, the meaning should be understood everywhere. The second [sutta] is of clear meaning.

3. Kumbhasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Kumbha Sutta

103. Tatiye kumbhāti ghaṭā. Tuccho pihitoti rittako pihitamukho. Pūro vivaṭoti udakapuṇṇo apārutamukho. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo.

103. In the third [sutta], 'pots' means jars. 'Empty and covered' means empty with its mouth covered. 'Full and open' means full of water with its mouth uncovered. This same method applies to the remaining two pairs.

4. Udakarahadasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Udakarahada Sutta

104. Catutthe uttāno gambhīrobhāsotiādīsu purāṇapaṇṇarasasambhinnavaṇṇo kāḷaudako gambhīrobhāso nāma, acchavippasannamaṇivaṇṇaudako uttānobhāso nāma.

104. In the fourth [sutta], regarding 'shallow with a deep appearance' and so forth: dark water, with a color mixed with the juice of old leaves, is what is called 'deep in appearance'; and water with the color of a clear, bright gem is what is called 'shallow in appearance'.

5-6. Ambasuttavaṇṇanā

5–6. Commentary on the Amba Sutta

105-6. Pañcame āmaṃ pakkavaṇṇīti āmakaṃ hutvā olokentānaṃ pakkasadisaṃ khāyati. Evaṃ sabbapadāni daṭṭhabbāni. Chaṭṭhaṃ uttānatthameva.

In the fifth [sutta], 'unripe with the appearance of being ripe' means that though it is unripe, to those who look at it, it appears to be like a ripe one. All the terms should be understood in this way. The sixth [sutta] is of clear meaning.

7. Mūsikasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Mūsika Sutta

107. Sattame [V 2.0323] yo āvāṭaṃ khaṇati, na ca tattha vasati, so gādhaṃ kattā no vasitāti vuccati. Khantātipi pāṭho. Iminā nayena sabbapadāni veditabbāni.

107. In the seventh [sutta], one who digs a pit but does not dwell there is called 'a maker of a firm place, not a dweller.' There is also the reading 'a digger.' By this method, all the terms should be understood.

8. Balībaddasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Balībadda Sutta

108. Aṭṭhame [M 2.0328] yo attano gogaṇaṃ maddati, na paragogaṇaṃ, ayaṃ sagavacaṇḍo no paragavacaṇḍoti evaṃ sabbapadāni veditabbāni. Ubbejetā hotīti ghaṭṭetvā vijjhitvā ubbegapattaṃ karoti.

108. In the eighth [sutta], an ox that oppresses its own herd of cattle, not another’s herd, is 'fierce towards its own herd, not fierce towards another's herd.' All the terms should be understood in this way. 'He is an agitator' means that by goading and piercing, he causes agitation.

9. Rukkhasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Rukkha Sutta

109. Navame pheggu phegguparivāroti nissāro pheggurukkho pheggurukkheheva parivuto. Sāraparivāroti [P 3.0120] khadirādīhi sārarukkheheva parivuto. Esa nayo sabbattha.

109. In the ninth [sutta], 'sapwood surrounded by sapwood' means a worthless sapwood tree surrounded only by sapwood trees. 'Heartwood surrounded by heartwood' means it is surrounded only by heartwood trees such as acacia. This is the method in all cases.

10. Āsīvisasuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Āsīvisa Sutta

110. Dasame āgataviso na ghoravisoti yassa visaṃ āgacchati, ghoraṃ pana na hoti, cirakālaṃ na pīḷeti. Sesapadesupi eseva nayoti.

110. In the tenth [discourse], 'venom that arrives but is not severe' means one whose venom arrives, but it is not severe and does not afflict for a long time. The same method applies to the remaining terms.

Valāhakavaggo paṭhamo.

The Chapter on Clouds is the first.

(12) 2. Kesivaggo

(12) 2. The Chapter on Kesī

1. Kesisuttavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Kesī Sutta

111. Dutiyassa [V 2.0324] paṭhame kesīti tassa nāmaṃ. Assadamme sāretīti assadammasārathi. Saṇhenapi vinetītiādīsu tassa anucchavikaṃ sakkāraṃ katvā subhojanaṃ bhojetvā madhurapānaṃ pāyetvā muduvacanena samudācaritvā damento saṇhena dameti nāma, jāṇubandhanamukhabandhanādīhi ceva patodavijjhanakasābhighātapharusavacanehi ca damento pharusena dameti nāma, kālena kālaṃ tadubhayaṃ karonto saṇhapharusena dameti nāma.

111. In the first [discourse] of the second [chapter], Kesī is his name. Assadammasārathi means one who trains horses to be tamed (assadamme sāreti). In the phrase 'saṇhenapi vineti' and so forth: one who tames by showing him appropriate respect, feeding him excellent food, giving him sweet drinks, and addressing him with gentle words, is said to tame gently. One who tames by binding his knees and mouth, and with goad-pricking, whip-striking, and harsh words, is said to tame harshly. One who does both at appropriate times is said to tame with gentleness and harshness.

2. Javasuttavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Java Sutta

112. Dutiye [M 2.0329] ajjavenāti ujukabhāvena. Javenāti padavegena. Khantiyāti adhivāsanakkhantiyā. Soraccenāti sucibhāvasīlena. Puggalaguṇaṅgesu javenāti ñāṇajavena. Sesamettha uttānatthameva.

112. In the second [discourse], ajjavenā means by straightforwardness, that is, by uprightness. Javenā means by speed, that is, by the speed of the feet. Khantiyā means by patience, that is, by the patience of endurance. Soraccenā means by gentleness, that is, by the virtue of pure conduct. In the context of personal qualities, javenā means by speed, that is, by the speed of wisdom. The rest here is clear in meaning.

3. Patodasuttavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Patoda Sutta

113. Tatiye [P 3.0121] patodacchāyanti vijjhanatthaṃ ukkhittassa patodassa chāyaṃ. Saṃvijjatīti “javo me gahetabbo”ti sallakkhaṇavasena saṃvijjati. Saṃvegaṃ āpajjatīti saṃvegaṃ paṭipajjati lomavedhaviddhoti lomakūpe patodavedhena viddhamatto. Cammavedhaviddhoti chavicammaṃ chindantena patodavedhena viddho. Aṭṭhivedhaviddhoti aṭṭhiṃ bhindantena vedhena viddho. Kāyenāti nāmakāyena. Paramasaccanti nibbānaṃ. Sacchikarotīti passati. Paññāyāti sahavipassanāya maggapaññāya.

113. In the third [discourse], patodacchāya means the shadow of the goad raised for striking. Saṃvijjati means it is perceived by noting, “I must take speed.” Saṃvegaṃ āpajjati means he attains urgency. Lomavedhaviddho means pierced by the goad’s strike into the hair pores. Cammavedhaviddho means pierced by the goad’s strike that cuts the hide. Aṭṭhivedhaviddho means pierced by the strike that breaks the bone. Kāyena means by the mental body. Paramasaccaṃ means Nibbāna. Sacchikaroti means he sees. Paññāya means by the wisdom of the path together with insight.

4. Nāgasuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Nāga Sutta

114. Catutthe [V 2.0325] aṭṭhiṃ katvāti aṭṭhiko hutvā. Tiṇavaninnādasaddānanti ettha tiṇavoti ḍiṇḍimo, ninnādasaddoti sabbesampi ekatomissito mahāsaddo. Ḍaṃsādīsu ḍaṃsāti piṅgalamakkhikā, makasā makasāva. Khippaññeva gantā hotīti sīlasamādhipaññāvimuttivimuttiñāṇadassanāni pūretvā sīghameva gantā hoti.

114. In the fourth [sutta], aṭṭhiṃ katvā means having become intent upon it (aṭṭhiko hutvā). Regarding tiṇavaninnādasaddāni: here tiṇavo means a kettledrum, and ninnādasaddo means a great sound mingled from all together. Among ḍaṃsādīsu (gadflies and so on): ḍaṃsā are reddish-brown flies, and makasā are mosquitoes. Khippaññeva gantā hoti means he goes very quickly; that is, by fulfilling virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation, he goes swiftly.

5. Ṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Ṭhāna Sutta

115. Pañcame ṭhānānīti kāraṇāni. Anatthāya saṃvattatīti ahitāya avaḍḍhiyā saṃvattati. Ettha ca paṭhamaṃ opātakkhaṇanamacchabandhanasandhicchedanādibhedaṃ sadukkhaṃ savighātaṃ pāpakammaṃ veditabbaṃ, dutiyaṃ samajīvikānaṃ gihīnaṃ pupphacchaḍḍakādikammaṃ sudhākoṭṭana-gehacchādanaasuciṭṭhānasammajjanādikammañca [P 3.0122] veditabbaṃ, tatiyaṃ surāpānagandhavilepanamālāpiḷandhanādikammañceva assādavasena pavattaṃ pāṇātipātādikammañca veditabbaṃ, catutthaṃ dhammassavanatthāya gamanakāle suddhavatthacchādana-mālāgandhādīnaṃ ādāya gamanaṃ [M 2.0330] cetiyavandanaṃ bodhivandanaṃ madhuradhammakathāsavanaṃ pañcasīlasamādānanti evamādīsu somanassasampayuttaṃ kusalakammaṃ veditabbaṃ. Purisathāmeti purisassa ñāṇathāmasmiṃ. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo.

115. In the fifth [sutta], 'grounds' (ṭhānāni) means reasons. Regarding 'anatthāya saṃvattati' (it leads to harm), it means it leads to detriment and decline. Here, the first should be understood as painful, destructive, and evil actions such as digging pitfalls, trapping fish, burglary, and so forth. The second should be understood as the actions of lay people living ordinary lives, such as the work of throwing away flowers, plastering walls, roofing houses, sweeping impure places, and so forth. The third should be understood as actions such as drinking alcohol, applying perfumes and cosmetics, wearing garlands, and so forth, driven by enjoyment, and actions such as killing living beings, and so forth. The fourth should be understood as wholesome actions accompanied by gladness, such as going to listen to the Dhamma, taking clean clothes, garlands, perfumes, and so forth, venerating shrines, venerating the Bodhi tree, listening to sweet Dhamma talks, and undertaking the five precepts, and so forth. 'Purisathāma' (a man's strength) means in a man's strength of wisdom. The same method applies to the remaining two.

6. Appamādasuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Appamāda Sutta

116. Chaṭṭhe yato khoti yadā kho. Samparāyikassāti desanāmattametaṃ, khīṇāsavo pana neva samparāyikassa, na diṭṭhadhammikassa maraṇassa bhāyati. Sova idha adhippeto. Keci pana “sammādiṭṭhi bhāvitāti vacanato sotāpannaṃ ādiṃ katvā sabbepi ariyā adhippetā”ti vadanti.

116. In the sixth [sutta], 'yato kho' means 'when indeed.' Regarding 'samparāyikassa' (of the next world), this is merely a teaching device. However, one whose taints are destroyed fears neither death in the next world nor death in this very life. He is the one intended here. Some, however, say that since the phrase 'right view is developed' is mentioned, all noble ones, beginning with stream-enterers, are intended.

7. Ārakkhasuttavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Ārakkha Sutta

117. Sattame attarūpenāti attano anurūpena anucchavikena, hitakāmenāti attho. Rajanīyesūti [V 2.0326] rāgassa paccayabhūtesu. Dhammesūti sabhāvesu, iṭṭhārammaṇesūti attho. Evaṃ sabbattha nayo veditabbo. Na rajjatīti diṭṭhivasena na rajjati. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Na ca pana samaṇavacanahetupi gacchatīti samaṇānaṃ paravādīnaṃ vacanahetupi attano diṭṭhiṃ pahāya tesaṃ diṭṭhivasena na gacchatīti attho. Idhāpi khīṇāsavova adhippeto.

117. In the seventh [sutta], 'attarūpena' means 'suitable and appropriate for oneself,' with the meaning of 'intending benefit.' Regarding 'rajanīyesū' (in enticing things), it refers to things that are conditions for lust. Regarding 'dhammesū' (in phenomena), it means in their intrinsic nature—that is, in desirable objects. This method should be understood in this way throughout. Regarding 'na rajjati' (does not lust), it means he does not lust based on views. The same method applies to the remaining phrases. Regarding 'na ca pana samaṇavacanahetupi gacchati' (nor does he go because of the words of ascetics), it means he does not abandon his own view and go according to the views of ascetics who are proponents of other doctrines because of their words. Here too, the one whose taints are destroyed is intended.

8-10. Saṃvejanīyādisuttattayavaṇṇanā

8-10. Commentary on the Three Suttas Beginning with the Saṃvejanīya Sutta

118-120. Aṭṭhame dassanīyānīti passitabbayuttakāni. Saṃvejanīyānīti saṃvegajanakāni. Navame jātibhayanti jātiṃ ārabbha uppajjanakabhayaṃ. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Dasame [P 3.0123] aggibhayanti aggiṃ paṭicca uppajjanakabhayaṃ. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.

118-120. In the eighth, 'dassanīyāni' means suitable to be seen. 'Saṃvejanīyāni' means productive of a sense of spiritual urgency. In the ninth, 'jātibhaya' means the fear that arises in connection with birth. The same method applies to the remaining terms. In the tenth, 'aggibhaya' means the fear that arises dependent on fire. The same method applies to the remaining terms.

Kesivaggo dutiyo.

The Kesī Chapter is the second.

(13) 3. Bhayavaggo

(13) 3. The Chapter on Fear

1. Attānuvādasuttavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Self-Reproach Sutta

121. Tatiyassa [V 2.0327][M 2.0331] paṭhame attānuvādabhayanti attānaṃ anuvadantassa uppajjanakabhayaṃ. Parānuvādabhayanti parassa anuvādato uppajjanakabhayaṃ. Daṇḍabhayanti dvattiṃsa kammakāraṇā paṭicca uppajjanakabhayaṃ. Duggatibhayanti cattāro apāye paṭicca uppajjanakabhayaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, attānuvādabhayantiādīsu attānuvādabhayaṃ tāva paccavekkhantassa ajjhattaṃ hirī samuṭṭhāti, sāssa tīsu dvāresu saṃvaraṃ janeti, tīsu dvāresu saṃvaro catupārisuddhisīlaṃ hoti. So tasmiṃ sīle patiṭṭhāya vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā aggaphale patiṭṭhāti. Parānuvādabhayaṃ pana paccavekkhantassa bahiddhā ottappaṃ samuṭṭhāti, tadassa tīsu dvāresu saṃvaraṃ janeti, tīsu dvāresu saṃvaro catupārisuddhisīlaṃ hoti. So tasmiṃ sīle patiṭṭhāya vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā aggaphale patiṭṭhāti. Duggatibhayaṃ paccavekkhantassa ajjhattaṃ hirī samuṭṭhāti, sāssa tīsu dvāresu saṃvaraṃ janeti, tīsu dvāresu saṃvaro catupārisuddhisīlaṃ hoti. So tasmiṃ sīle patiṭṭhāya vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā aggaphale patiṭṭhāti.

121. In the first sutta of the third vagga, 'attānuvādabhaya' (the fear of self-reproach) means the fear that arises for one who reproaches oneself. 'Parānuvādabhaya' (the fear of others' reproach) means the fear that arises from the reproach of another. 'Daṇḍabhaya' (the fear of punishment) means the fear that arises dependent on the thirty-two grounds for punishment. 'Duggatibhaya' (the fear of a woeful destination) means the fear that arises dependent on the four woeful states. Regarding the passage beginning, 'This, monks, is called the fear of self-reproach,' for one who reflects on the fear of self-reproach, moral shame (hirī) arises internally. This generates restraint in the three doors, and restraint in the three doors constitutes the fourfold purification virtue. Established in that virtue, one develops insight and becomes established in the path and fruit. For one who reflects on the fear of others' reproach, moral dread (ottappa) arises externally. This generates restraint in the three doors, and restraint in the three doors constitutes the fourfold purification virtue. Established in that virtue, one develops insight and becomes established in the highest fruit. For one who reflects on the fear of a woeful destination, moral shame (hirī) arises internally. This generates restraint in the three doors, and restraint in the three doors constitutes the fourfold purification virtue. Established in that virtue, one develops insight and becomes established in the highest fruit.

2. Ūmibhayasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Discourse on the Fear of Waves

122. Dutiye udakorohantassāti udakaṃ otarantassa. Pāṭikaṅkhitabbānīti icchitabbāni. Susukābhayanti caṇḍamacchabhayaṃ. Mukhāvaraṇaṃ maññe karontīti mukhapidahanaṃ viya karonti. Odarikattassāti [P 3.0124] mahodaratāya mahagghasabhāvassa. Arakkhiteneva kāyenātiādīsu kāyadvāre tividhassa saṃvarassa abhāvato arakkhitena kāyena. Vacīdvāre catubbidhassa saṃvarassa abhāvato arakkhitāya vācāya.

122. In the second sutta, 'for one descending into the water' means for one going down into the water. 'To be expected' means to be desired. 'The fear of sharks' means the fear of fierce fish. 'They seem to cover the mouth' means they act as if covering the mouth. 'Due to being gluttonous' means due to having a large belly and a very greedy nature. In the passage beginning 'With an unprotected body,' this means with a body unprotected due to the absence of threefold restraint at the bodily door. 'With unprotected speech' means with speech unprotected due to the absence of fourfold restraint at the verbal door.

3. Paṭhamanānākaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the First Discourse on Diversity

123. Tatiye tadassādetīti taṃ jhānaṃ sukhassādena assādeti. Nikāmetīti pattheti. Vittiṃ [V 2.0328] āpajjatīti tuṭṭhiṃ āpajjati. Tadadhimuttoti [M 2.0332] tasmiṃ adhimutto, taṃ vā adhimutto. Tabbahulavihārīti tena jhānena bahulaṃ viharanto. Sahabyataṃ upapajjatīti sahabhāvaṃ gacchati, tattha nibbattatīti attho. Kappo āyuppamāṇanti ettha paṭhamajjhānaṃ atthi hīnaṃ, atthi majjhimaṃ, atthi paṇītaṃ. Tattha hīnena uppannānaṃ kappassa tatiyo koṭṭhāso āyuppamāṇaṃ, majjhimena upaḍḍhakappo, paṇītena kappo. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Nirayampi gacchatīti nirayagamanīyassa kammassa appahīnattā aparāparaṃ gacchati, na anantarameva. Tasmiṃyeva bhave parinibbāyatīti tasmiṃyeva rūpabhave ṭhatvā parinibbāyati, na heṭṭhā otarati. Yadidaṃ gatiyā upapattiyā satīti yaṃ idaṃ gatiyā ca upapattiyā ca sati sekhassa ariyasāvakassa paṭisandhivasena heṭṭhā anotaritvā tasmiṃyeva rūpabhave upari dutiyatatiyādīsu aññatarasmiṃ brahmaloke parinibbānaṃ, puthujjanassa pana nirayādigamanaṃ, idaṃ nānākaraṇanti attho.

123. In the third sutta, 'he relishes it' means he relishes that jhāna with the flavor of bliss. 'He desires it' means he longs for it. 'He delights in it' means he attains delight. 'Intent on that' means intent on that jhāna, or inclined toward it. 'Dwelling much in it' means frequently dwelling in that jhāna. 'He is reborn in companionship' means he goes to companionship, that is, he is reborn there. Regarding 'The lifespan is an eon,' here the first jhāna is of three kinds: inferior, middling, and superior. For those reborn through the inferior, the lifespan is a third of an eon; for the middling, half an eon; for the superior, an eon. This was said in reference to that. 'He may also go to hell' means he goes again and again, not immediately, due to not abandoning the kamma leading to hell. 'He attains final nibbāna in that very existence' means he attains final nibbāna while remaining in that very form existence, without descending lower. 'That is, in terms of destination and rebirth' means this refers to the fact that, given a destination and rebirth, a noble disciple in training does not descend lower by way of rebirth, but attains final nibbāna in that very form existence or in a higher Brahma world, such as the second or third; whereas an ordinary person may go to hell or other destinations. This is the distinction.

Dve kappāti etthāpi dutiyajjhānaṃ vuttanayeneva tividhaṃ hoti. Tattha paṇītabhāvanena nibbattānaṃ aṭṭhakappā āyuppamāṇaṃ, majjhimena cattāro, hīnena dve. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Cattāro [P 3.0125] kappāti ettha yaṃ heṭṭhā vuttaṃ “kappo, dve kappā”ti, tampi āharitvā attho veditabbo. Kappoti ca guṇassapi nāmaṃ, tasmā kappo dve kappā cattāro kappāti ayamettha attho daṭṭhabbo.
