Because it 'sinks' (sīdati), it is called 'sata'; this is a designation for the impermanent. Therefore, they should be understood as stated by way of eternalism and annihilationism. The four terms that follow these, beginning with 'santi', are stated by way of doubt and speculation. In such phrases as 'santi hoti', the meaning should be understood as 'Might I be?'. The intention here should be grasped in the same way as stated in the previous tetrad. Furthermore, the four terms beginning with 'apihaṃ santi' are stated by way of longing and imagining, thus: 'Would that I might be!'. These too should be understood in the same way as stated in the previous tetrad. As for the four terms beginning with 'bhavissanti', they are stated by way of the future. The meaning of these also should be understood in the same way as stated in the previous tetrad. Thus, among these—

“Dve diṭṭhisīsā sīsaññe, cattāro sīsamūlakā;

Tayo tayoti etāni, aṭṭhārasa vibhāvaye.

Two are heads of views, four others are heads; three each are rooted in the heads. Thus should one make clear these eighteen.

Etesu hi asasmi, satasmīti ete dve diṭṭhisīsā nāma. Asmi, santi, apihaṃ santi, bhavissanti ete cattāro suddhasīsā eva. Itthasmītiādayo tayo tayoti dvādasa sīsamūlakā nāmāti evamete dve diṭṭhisīsā cattāro suddhasīsā dvādasa sīsamūlakāti aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritadhammā veditabbā. Imāni tāva ajjhattikassa upādāya aṭṭhārasa taṇhāvicaritāni. Bāhirassa upādāya taṇhāvicaritesupi eseva [M 2.0388] nayo. Imināti iminā rūpena vā…pe… viññāṇena vāti esa viseso veditabbo. Sesaṃ tādisameva.

Among these, 'I am permanent' and 'I am perishable' are called the two heads of views. 'I am', 'I might be', 'Would that I might be!', and 'I will be'—these four are indeed mere heads. The three each beginning with 'I am thus', thus twelve, are called those rooted in the heads. Thus, these two heads of views, four mere heads, and twelve rooted in the heads—in this way, the eighteen phenomena of the roamings of craving should be understood. These, to begin with, are the eighteen roamings of craving with reference to the internal. With reference to the external, for the roamings of craving, this is the same method. 'By this' means 'by this form...' or '...by this consciousness'—this distinction should be understood. The remainder is just the same.

Iti evarūpāni atītāni chattiṃsāti ekamekassa puggalassa atīte addhani chattiṃsa. Anāgatāni [V 2.0384] chattiṃsāti ekamekasseva puggalassa ca anāgate addhani chattiṃsa. Paccuppannāni chattiṃsāti ekassa vā puggalassa yathāsambhavato bahūnaṃ vā paccuppanne addhani chattiṃsāva. Sabbasattānaṃ pana niyameneva atīte addhani chattiṃsa, anāgate chattiṃsa, paccuppanne chattiṃsa. Anantā hi asadisataṇhāmānadiṭṭhibhedā sattā. Aṭṭhasataṃ [P 3.0209] taṇhāvicaritaṃ hontīti ettha pana aṭṭhasatasaṅkhātaṃ taṇhāvicaritaṃ hotīti evamattho daṭṭhabbo.

Thus, 'thirty-six such [roamings of craving] in the past' means thirty-six for each individual in the past time. 'Thirty-six in the future' means thirty-six for each and every individual in the future time. 'Thirty-six in the present' means thirty-six for one individual, or for many as is possible, in the present time. Furthermore, for all beings, it is invariably thirty-six in the past time, thirty-six in the future, and thirty-six in the present. For beings are infinite, differentiated by dissimilar craving, conceit, and views. But here, regarding the statement 'one hundred and eight roamings of craving occur,' the meaning should be understood thus: the roaming of craving, reckoned as one hundred and eight, occurs.

10. Pemasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Pemasutta

200. Dasame na ussenetīti diṭṭhivasena na ukkhipati. Na paṭisenetīti paṭiviruddho hutvā kalahabhaṇḍanavasena na ukkhipati. Na dhūpāyatīti ajjhattikassa upādāya taṇhāvicaritavasena na dhūpāyati. Na pajjalatīti bāhirassa upādāya taṇhāvicaritavasena na pajjalati. Na sampajjhāyatīti asmimānavasena na sampajjhāyati. Sesaṃ pāḷinayeneva veditabbaṃ. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitanti.

200. In the tenth, 'does not exalt' means does not lift up by way of views. 'Does not oppose' means, having become opposed, does not lift up by way of quarreling and disputing. 'Does not smolder' means does not smolder with reference to the internal by way of the roamings of craving. 'Does not blaze' means does not blaze with reference to the external by way of the roamings of craving. 'Does not brood' means does not brood by way of the conceit 'I am'. The rest is to be understood in accordance with the method of the Pāḷi. In this sutta, the round of existence and its cessation have been spoken about.

Mahāvaggo pañcamo.

The Great Chapter, the Fifth.

Catutthapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Fifty is Finished.

5. Pañcamapaṇṇāsakaṃ

5. The Fifth Fifty

(21) 1. Sappurisavaggo

(21) 1. The Chapter on the Worthy Person

1-6. Sikkhāpadasuttavaṇṇanā

1-6. Commentary on the Sikkhāpadasutta

201. Pañcamassa [V 2.0385][M 2.0389] paṭhame asappurisanti lāmakapurisaṃ tucchapurisaṃ mūḷhapurisaṃ avijjāya andhīkataṃ bālaṃ. Asappurisataranti atirekena asappurisaṃ. Itare dve vuttapaṭipakkhavasena veditabbā. Sesamettha uttānatthameva. Yathā cettha, evaṃ ito paresu pañcasu. Etesu hi paṭhamaṃ pañcaveravasena desitaṃ, dutiyaṃ assaddhammavasena, tatiyaṃ kāyavacīdvāravasena, catutthaṃ manodvāravasena, pañcamaṃ aṭṭhamicchattavasena, chaṭṭhaṃ dasamicchattavasena.

201. In the first of the fifth, 'unworthy person' means a base person, a worthless person, a deluded person, a fool made blind by ignorance. 'A more unworthy person' means one who is exceedingly an unworthy person. The other two are to be understood by way of the opposite of what has been stated. The rest here is of obvious meaning. As it is here, so it is in the following five suttas. For in these, the first is taught by way of the five enmities, the second by way of the qualities of the unworthy, the third by way of the bodily and verbal doors, the fourth by way of the mental door, the fifth by way of the eight wrongnesses, and the sixth by way of the ten wrongnesses.

7-10. Pāpadhammasuttacatukkavaṇṇanā

7-10. Commentary on the Pāpadhammasutta Group

207-210. Sattame [P 3.0210] pāpanti lāmakaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhapuggalaṃ. Kalyāṇanti bhaddakaṃ anavajjapuggalaṃ. Sesamettha uttānatthameva. Aṭṭhamepi eseva nayo. Navame pāpadhammanti lāmakadhammaṃ. Kalyāṇadhammanti anavajjadhammaṃ. Sesamettha uttānatthameva. Dasamepi eseva nayo. Imasmiṃ vagge dasasupi suttesu agāriyappaṭipadā kathitā. Sacepi sotāpannasakadāgāmino honti, vaṭṭatiyevāti.

In the seventh sutta, 'evil' means a base, defiled person. 'Good' means an excellent, blameless person. The rest here has an obvious meaning. The same method applies to the eighth sutta as well. In the ninth sutta, 'one of evil nature' means a person of base nature. 'One of good nature' means a person of blameless nature. The rest here has an obvious meaning. The same method applies to the tenth sutta as well. In this chapter, in all ten suttas, the practice of a householder is taught. Even if they are stream-enterers or once-returners, it is indeed fitting.

Sappurisavaggo paṭhamo.

The Chapter on the Good Person, the First.

(22) 2. Parisāvaggo

(22) 2. The Chapter on Assemblies

1. Parisāsuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Suttas on Assemblies

211. Dutiyassa [V 2.0386] paṭhame parisaṃ dūsentīti parisadūsanā. Parisaṃ sobhentīti parisasobhanā.

211. In the first sutta of the second chapter: They are 'corrupters of the assembly' because they corrupt the assembly. They are 'adorners of the assembly' because they adorn the assembly.

2. Diṭṭhisuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Sutta on Views

212. Dutiye manoduccarite pariyāpannāpi micchādiṭṭhi mahāsāvajjatāya visuṃ vuttā, tassā ca paṭipakkhavasena sammādiṭṭhi.

212. In the second sutta, wrong view, although included in mental misconduct, is mentioned separately because of its great blameworthiness; and right view is mentioned by way of its opposite.

3. Akataññutāsuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Sutta on Ingratitude

213. Tatiye [M 2.0390] akataññutā akataveditāti akataññutāya akataveditāya. Ubhayampetaṃ atthato ekameva. Sukkapakkhepi eseva nayo.

213. In the third sutta, 'ingratitude and ungratefulness' is a compound of 'ingratitude' and 'ungratefulness'. Both of these terms are one and the same in meaning. The same method applies to the bright side as well.

4-7. Pāṇātipātīsuttādivaṇṇanā

4–7. Commentary on the Sutta on Killing Living Beings and others

214-217. Catutthaṃ catunnaṃ kammakilesānaṃ tappaṭipakkhassa ca vasena vuttaṃ, pañcamaṃ sukkapakkhānaṃ ādito catunnaṃ micchattānaṃ vasena, chaṭṭhaṃ avasesānaṃ catunnaṃ, sattamaṃ anariyavohāraariyavohārānaṃ. Tathā [P 3.0211] aṭṭhamanavamadasamāni sappaṭipakkhānaṃ assaddhammānaṃ vasena vuttāni. Sabbasuttesu pana sukkapakkhadhammā lokiyalokuttaramissakāva kathitā. Navasu suttesu kiñcāpi “sagge”ti vuttaṃ, tayo pana maggā tīṇi ca phalāni labbhantiyevāti.

The fourth sutta is taught by way of the four defilements of action and their opposites. The fifth is taught by way of the first four wrongnesses. The sixth is taught by way of the remaining four wrongnesses. The seventh is taught by way of ignoble and noble expressions. Similarly, the eighth is taught in the same way. The ninth and tenth are taught by way of the qualities of the untrue person and their opposites. However, in all the suttas, the bright-side qualities are taught as mixed, being both mundane and supramundane. Although in nine suttas it is said 'in heaven', nevertheless the three paths and three fruits are indeed attained.

Parisāvaggo dutiyo.

The Chapter on the Assembly, the Second.

(23) 3. Duccaritavaggavaṇṇanā

(23) 3. Commentary on the Chapter on Misconduct

221-231. Tatiyassa [V 2.0387] paṭhamādīni uttānatthāneva. Dasame yo cintetvā kabyaṃ karoti, ayaṃ cintākavi nāma. Yo sutvā karoti, ayaṃ sutakavi nāma. Yo ekaṃ atthaṃ nissāya karoti, ayaṃ atthakavi nāma. Yo taṅkhaṇaññeva vaṅgīsatthero viya attano paṭibhānena karoti, ayaṃ paṭibhānakavi nāmāti.

The commentaries on the first and following suttas of the third chapter are of obvious meaning. In the tenth sutta: one who composes poetry after reflection is called a reflective poet. One who composes after having heard is called a learned poet. One who composes based on a single theme is called a thematic poet. One who composes spontaneously at that very moment by his own ready wit, like the Elder Vaṅgīsa, is called an inspired poet.

Duccaritavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on Misconduct, the Third.

(24) 4. Kammavaggo

(24) 4. The Chapter on Kamma

1. Saṃkhittasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Concise Sutta

232. Catutthassa [V 2.0388] paṭhame kaṇhanti kāḷakaṃ dasaakusalakammapathakammaṃ. Kaṇhavipākanti apāye nibbattanato kāḷakavipākaṃ. Sukkanti paṇḍarakaṃ kusalakammapathakammaṃ[M 2.0391]. Sukkavipākanti sagge nibbattanato paṇḍarakavipākaṃ. Kaṇhasukkanti missakakammaṃ. Kaṇhasukkavipākanti [P 3.0212] sukhadukkhavipākaṃ. Missakakammañhi katvā akusalena tiracchānayoniyaṃ maṅgalahatthiṭṭhānādīsu uppanno kusalena pavatte sukhaṃ vediyati. Kusalena rājakulepi nibbatto akusalena pavatte dukkhaṃ vediyati. Akaṇhaṃ asukkanti kammakkhayakaraṃ catumaggañāṇaṃ adhippetaṃ. Tañhi yadi kaṇhaṃ bhaveyya, kaṇhavipākaṃ dadeyya. Yadi sukkaṃ bhaveyya, sukkavipākaṃ dadeyya. Ubhayavipākassa pana appadānato akaṇhaṃ asukkanti ayamettha attho.

232. In the first sutta of the fourth chapter, 'dark' refers to the kamma of the ten unwholesome courses of action. 'Dark result' means the dark result from being reborn in the planes of misery. 'Bright' refers to the kamma of the ten wholesome courses of action. 'Bright result' means the bright result from being reborn in a heavenly world. 'Dark-bright' refers to mixed kamma. 'Dark-bright result' means a result of pleasure and pain. Indeed, having performed mixed kamma, one might be reborn in the animal realm—in a position such as that of an auspicious elephant—due to the unwholesome portion, yet experience pleasure in the course of that life due to the wholesome portion. Due to the wholesome portion, one might also be born in a royal family, yet experience suffering in the course of that life due to the unwholesome portion. By 'neither dark nor bright' is intended the knowledge of the four paths that brings about the destruction of kamma. Indeed, if that knowledge were dark, it would yield a dark result; if it were bright, it would yield a bright result. However, because it does not give a result of both kinds, it is 'neither dark nor bright.' This is the meaning here.

2. Vitthārasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Detailed Sutta

233. Dutiye sabyābajjhanti sadosaṃ. Kāyasaṅkhāranti kāyadvāracetanaṃ. Abhisaṅkharotīti āyūhati sampiṇḍeti. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo. Sabyābajjhaṃ lokanti sadukkhaṃ lokaṃ. Sabyābajjhā phassāti sadukkhā vipākaphassā. Sabyābajjhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyatīti sābādhaṃ vipākavedanaṃ vediyati. Ekantadukkhanti ekanteneva dukkhaṃ, na sukhasammissaṃ. Seyyathāpi sattā nerayikāti ettha seyyathāpīti nidassanatthe nipāto. Tena kevalaṃ nerayikasatte dasseti, aññe pana taṃsarikkhakā nāma natthi. Iminā upāyena sabbattha attho veditabbo. Seyyathāpi manussātiādīsu pana manussānaṃ tāva kālena sukhā vedanā uppajjati, kālena dukkhā vedanā. Ekacce [P 3.0213] ca devāti ettha pana kāmāvacaradevā daṭṭhabbā. Tesañhi mahesakkhatarā devatā disvā nisinnāsanato vuṭṭhānaṃ, pārutauttarāsaṅgassa otāraṇaṃ, añjalipaggaṇhanantiādīnaṃ vasena kālena dukkhaṃ uppajjati, dibbasampattiṃ anubhavantānaṃ kālena sukhaṃ. Ekacce ca vinipātikāti ettha vemānikapetā daṭṭhabbā. Te nirantarameva ekasmiṃ kāle sukhaṃ, ekasmiṃ kāle [V 2.0389] dukkhaṃ vediyanti. Nāgasupaṇṇahatthiassādayo pana manussā viya vokiṇṇasukhadukkhāva honti. Pahānāya yā cetanāti ettha vivaṭṭagāminī maggacetanā veditabbā. Sā hi kammakkhayāya saṃvattatīti.

233. In the second sutta: 'With affliction' means with fault. 'Bodily formation' means volition at the body-door. 'He forms' means he strives and accumulates. This same method applies to the other two. 'A world with affliction' means a world with suffering. 'Contacts with affliction' means resultant contacts with suffering. 'He experiences a feeling with affliction' means he experiences a resultant feeling that is painful. 'Exclusively painful' means entirely painful, not mixed with pleasure. In the phrase 'just as beings in hell', the word 'just as' is a particle for the purpose of illustration. Thus it indicates only beings in hell, for there are no others exactly like them. The meaning should be understood in this way everywhere. Furthermore, in phrases such as 'just as humans', for humans a pleasant feeling arises at one time and a painful feeling at another time. And in the phrase 'and certain devas', devas of the sense-sphere should be understood. Indeed, for them, suffering sometimes arises—on account of seeing more powerful deities and having to rise from their seats, lower their upper robes, raise their hands in homage, and so on—while at other times, when experiencing their divine fortune, pleasure arises. And in the phrase 'and certain beings in the fallen state', mansion-dwelling petas should be understood. They continuously experience pleasure at one time and suffering at another. As for nāgas, supaṇṇas, elephants, horses, and so on, like humans they experience a mixture of pleasure and pain. In the phrase 'the volition for abandoning', the path-volition leading away from the round of existence should be understood, for it leads to the destruction of kamma.

3. Soṇakāyanasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Sutta to Soṇakāyana

234. Tatiye [M 2.0392] sikhāmoggallānoti sīsamajjhe ṭhitāya mahatiyā sikhāya samannāgato moggallānagotto brāhmaṇo. Purimānīti atītānantaradivasato paṭṭhāya purimāni, dutiyādito paṭṭhāya purimatarāni veditabbāni. Soṇakāyanoti tasseva antevāsiko. Kammasaccāyaṃ bho lokoti bho ayaṃ loko kammasabhāvo. Kammasamārambhaṭṭhāyīti kammasamārambhena tiṭṭhati. Kammaṃ āyūhantova tiṭṭhati, anāyūhanto ucchijjatīti dīpeti. Sesaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva.

234. In the third sutta: Sikhā Moggallāna is a brahmin of the Moggallāna clan who possesses a large topknot situated in the middle of his head. 'Previous' means the days starting from the one immediately past; 'more previous' should be understood as those starting from the second day back, and so on. Soṇakāyana was his pupil. 'Sir, this world has kamma as its truth' means: 'Sir, this world has kamma as its nature.' 'One who subsists by the undertaking of kamma' means one subsists through the undertaking of kamma. This indicates that one subsists only by undertaking kamma; by not undertaking it, one is cut off. The rest is just in the manner stated above.

4-9. Sikkhāpadasuttādivaṇṇanā

4–9. Commentary on the Suttas on the Training Rules, etc.

235. Catutthādīnipi uttānatthāneva. Maggaṅgesu pana yasmā satiyā upaṭṭhapetvā paññāya paricchindati, tasmā ubhayameva kammaṃ. Sesā aṅgāneva honti, no kammanti [P 3.0214] vuttaṃ. Bojjhaṅgesupi eseva nayo. Abhidhamme pana sabbampetaṃ avisesena cetanāsampayuttakammanteva vaṇṇitaṃ.

235. The fourth sutta and the following ones also have an obvious meaning. As to the path factors, since one establishes mindfulness and then discerns with wisdom, both of these are kamma. It is said that the remaining factors are merely factors, not kamma. The same principle applies to the enlightenment factors. In the Abhidhamma, however, all of these are described without distinction as kamma associated with volition.

10. Samaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Samaṇa Sutta

241. Dasame idhevāti imasmiṃyeva sāsane. Ayaṃ pana niyamo sesapadesupi veditabbo. Dutiyādayopi hi samaṇā idheva, na aññattha. Suññāti rittā tucchā. Parappavādāti cattāro sassatavādā, cattāro ekaccasassatikā, cattāro antānantikā, cattāro amarāvikkhepikā, dve adhiccasamuppannikā, soḷasa saññivādā, aṭṭha asaññivādā, aṭṭha nevasaññināsaññivādā, satta ucchedavādā, pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādāti ime sabbepi brahmajāle āgatadvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhiyo ito bāhirānaṃ paresaṃ pavādā parappavādā nāma. Te sabbepi imehi catūhi phalaṭṭhakasamaṇehi suññā. Na hi te ettha santi. Na kevalañca eteheva suññā[V 2.0390], catūhi pana maggaṭṭhakasamaṇehipi, catunnaṃ maggānaṃ atthāya āraddhavipassakehipīti dvādasahipi samaṇehi suññā eva. Idameva atthaṃ sandhāya bhagavatā mahāparinibbāne (dī. ni. 2.214) vuttaṃ –

241. In the tenth sutta: 'Here only' means within this very Dispensation. This principle should be understood to apply to the remaining terms as well. Indeed, the second and subsequent ascetics are also found here only, not elsewhere. 'Empty' means void, hollow. 'Doctrines of others' refers to all these sixty-two views that come in the Brahmajāla Sutta: the four eternalist views, the four partial-eternalist views, the four views on finitude and infinitude, the four evasive prevarications, the two views of fortuitous origination, the sixteen perceptionist views, the eight non-perceptionist views, the eight neither-perceptionist-nor-non-perceptionist views, the seven annihilationist views, and the five views on Nibbāna in this very life. These doctrines of others who are outside this Dispensation are called 'doctrines of others.' All of them are empty of these four ascetics established in the fruit, for they are not found there. And they are empty not only of these, but indeed also of the four ascetics established in the path and of those who have undertaken insight for the sake of the four paths—thus they are empty of all twelve kinds of ascetics indeed. It is with reference to this very meaning that the Blessed One said in the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta:

“Ekūnatiṃso [M 2.0393] vayasā subhadda,

Yaṃ pabbajiṃ kiṃkusalānuesī;

Vassāni paññāsa samādhikāni,

Yato ahaṃ pabbajito subhadda;

Ñāyassa dhammassa padesavattī,

Ito bahiddhā samaṇopi natthi”.

“O Subhadda, at twenty-nine years of age, I went forth seeking what is wholesome. O Subhadda, since I went forth, more than fifty years have passed. Outside of this Dispensation, there is not even an ascetic who is a partial practitioner of the Dhamma of the method.”

“Dutiyopi samaṇo natthi, tatiyopi samaṇo natthi, catutthopi samaṇo natthi, suññā parappavādā samaṇehi aññehī”ti[P 3.0215]. Ettha hi padesavattīti āraddhavipassako adhippeto. Tasmā sotāpattimaggassa āraddhavipassakaṃ maggaṭṭhaṃ phalaṭṭhanti tayopi ekato katvā “samaṇopi natthī”ti āha, sakadāgāmimaggassa āraddhavipassakaṃ maggaṭṭhaṃ phalaṭṭhanti tayopi ekato katvā “dutiyopi samaṇo natthī”ti āha. Itaresupi dvīsu eseva nayo. Ekādasamaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

“There is no second ascetic, there is no third ascetic, there is no fourth ascetic. The doctrines of others are empty of ascetics.” Here, by 'partial practitioner' is intended one who has undertaken insight. Therefore, grouping together as one these three—the one who has undertaken insight for the path of stream-entry, the one established in the path, and the one established in the fruit—He said: “there is no ascetic.” Grouping together as one these three—the one who has undertaken insight for the path of the once-returner, the one established in the path, and the one established in the fruit—He said: “there is no second ascetic.” This same method applies to the other two cases. The eleventh sutta has an obvious meaning indeed.

Kammavaggo catuttho.

The Kamma Chapter, the Fourth.

(25) 5. Āpattibhayavaggo

(25) 5. The Chapter on the Danger of Offenses

1. Saṅghabhedakasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on Schism in the Sangha

243. Pañcamassa [V 2.0391] paṭhame api nu taṃ, ānanda, adhikaraṇanti vivādādhikaraṇādīsu aññataraṃ adhikaraṇaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa uppajji, satthā tassa vūpasantabhāvaṃ pucchanto evamāha. Kuto taṃ, bhanteti, bhante, kuto kinti kena kāraṇena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamissatīti vadati. Kevalakappanti sakalaṃ samantato. Saṅghabhedāya ṭhitoti saṅghena saddhiṃ vādatthāya kathitaṃ paṭikathentova ṭhito. Tatrāyasmāti tasmiṃ evaṃ ṭhite āyasmā anuruddho. Na ekavācikampi bhaṇitabbaṃ maññatīti “mā, āvuso, saṅghena saddhiṃ evaṃ avacā”ti ekavacanampi vattabbaṃ na maññati. Voyuñjatīti anuyuñjati anuyogaṃ āpajjati. Atthavaseti kāraṇavase. Nāsessantīti [P 3.0216] uposathappavāraṇaṃ upagantuṃ adatvā nikkaḍḍhissanti. Sesaṃ pāḷivaseneva veditabbaṃ.

243. In the first sutta of the fifth chapter: a legal issue, one of those beginning with disputes, had arisen in the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. The Teacher, inquiring about its settlement, said, 'Has that legal issue, Ānanda...?'. 'From where, venerable sir?' (`Kuto taṃ, bhante`): he asks, 'From what cause will that legal issue be settled?'. Completely (`kevalakappaṃ`): entirely, on all sides. Standing for schism in the Saṅgha (`saṅghabhedāya ṭhito`): he stands opposing what was said with the Saṅgha for the purpose of settling the legal issue. Therein the venerable one (`tatrāyasmā`): while he was standing thus, the Venerable Anuruddha. He does not think even a single word should be spoken: he does not think that even a single utterance such as, 'Friend, do not speak thus with the Saṅgha,' should be said. Engages (`voyuñjatīti`): he strives, he strives again and again, he undertakes the effort. For a reason (`atthavase`): due to a cause. They will bring to ruin (`nāsessanti`): they will expel him by not giving him permission to attend the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā. The rest should be understood in accordance with the canonical text.

2. Āpattibhayasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Discourse on the Danger of an Offense

244. Dutiye [M 2.0394] khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvāti pañca sikhaṇḍake ṭhapetvā khurena muṇḍaṃ karitvā. Kharassarenāti kakkhaḷasaddena. Paṇavenāti vajjhabheriyā. Thalaṭṭhassāti ekamante ṭhitassa. Sīsacchejjanti sīsacchedārahaṃ. Yatra hi nāmāti yaṃ nāma. So vatassāhanti so vata ahaṃ assaṃ, yaṃ evarūpaṃ pāpaṃ na kareyyanti attho. Yathādhammaṃ paṭikarissatīti dhammānurūpaṃ paṭikarissati, sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ ṭhassatīti attho. Kāḷavatthaṃ paridhāyāti kāḷapilotikaṃ nivāsetvā. Mosallanti musalābhipātārahaṃ. Yathādhammanti idha āpattito vuṭṭhāya suddhante patiṭṭhahanto yathādhammaṃ karoti nāma. Bhasmapuṭanti chārikābhaṇḍikaṃ. Gārayhaṃ bhasmapuṭanti garahitabbachārikāpuṭena matthake abhighātārahaṃ. Yathādhammanti idha āpattiṃ desento yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti nāma. Upavajjanti upavādārahaṃ. Pāṭidesanīyesūti paṭidesetabbesu. Iminā [P 3.0217] sabbāpi [V 2.0392] sesāpattiyo saṅgahitā. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri āpattibhayānīti, bhikkhave, imāni cattāri āpattiṃ nissāya uppajjanakabhayāni nāmāti.

244. In the second sutta: Having made the head bald with a razor means leaving five topknots and having made the head bald with a razor. With a harsh voice means with a rough sound. With a drum means with a drum narrow in the middle. Of one standing aside means of one standing to one side. Worthy of beheading means deserving to have the head cut off. `Yatra hi nāma` means `yaṃ nāma`. `So vatassāhaṃ` means: the meaning is, 'Surely, I would be one who would not commit such an evil deed.' He will make amends in accordance with the Dhamma: the meaning is that he will make amends in a way that is consistent with the Dhamma; he will be established on the level of a novice. Having put on a black garment means having caused him to wear a black, worn-out cloth. Worthy of a pestle means deserving to be struck with a pestle. According to the Dhamma: here, this refers to a monk who, having risen from an offense, establishes himself in purity and thus is called one who acts according to the Dhamma. A bundle of ashes means a small bundle of ash. A contemptible bundle of ashes means deserving to be rubbed on the head with a blameworthy bundle of ash. According to the Dhamma: here, this refers to a monk who confesses an offense and thus is called one who makes amends according to the Dhamma. Blameworthy means deserving of censure. In the offenses to be acknowledged means in those that must be acknowledged. By this, all remaining offenses are included. These, Bhikkhus, are the four dangers of offenses: this means, 'Bhikkhus, these four are called dangers that arise in dependence on an offense.'

3. Sikkhānisaṃsasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Discourse on the Benefits of the Training

245. Tatiye sikkhā ānisaṃsā etthāti sikkhānisaṃsaṃ. Paññā uttarā etthāti paññuttaraṃ. Vimutti sāro etthāti vimuttisāraṃ. Sati ādhipateyyā etthāti satādhipateyyaṃ. Etesaṃ hi sikkhādisaṅkhātānaṃ ānisaṃsādīnaṃ atthāya vussatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Ābhisamācārikāti uttamasamācārikā. Vattavasena paññattasīlassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tathā tathā so tassā sikkhāyāti tathā tathā so sikkhākāmo bhikkhu tasmiṃ sikkhāpade.

245. In the third sutta: Having the benefits of the training (`sikkhānisaṃsaṃ`): the benefits of the training are in this. Having wisdom as supreme (`paññuttaraṃ`): wisdom is supreme in this. Having liberation as its essence (`vimuttisāraṃ`): liberation, called the fruit of Arahantship, is the essence in this. Having mindfulness as its governing principle (`satādhipateyyaṃ`): mindfulness is the governing principle in this. For it is said that one lives the holy life for the sake of these—the benefits and so on, of what is designated as the training and so on. Of proper conduct (`ābhisamācārikā`) means of the highest conduct. This is a designation for the virtue prescribed in terms of duties. Thus, in that way, for that training: this means, 'in that way, that bhikkhu who is desirous of training applies himself to that training rule.'

Ādibrahmacariyikāti maggabrahmacariyassa ādibhūtānaṃ catunnaṃ mahāsīlānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Sabbasoti sabbākārena. Dhammāti catusaccadhammā. Paññāya samavekkhitā hontīti sahavipassanāya maggapaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti. Vimuttiyā phusitā hontīti arahattaphalavimuttiyā ñāṇaphassena phuṭṭhā honti. Ajjhattaṃyeva sati sūpaṭṭhitā hotīti niyakajjhatteyeva sati suṭṭhu upaṭṭhitā hoti. Paññāya anuggahessāmīti vipassanāpaññāya [M 2.0395] anuggahessāmi. Paññāya [P 3.0218] samavekkhissāmīti idhāpi vipassanāpaññā adhippetā. Phusitaṃ vā dhammaṃ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmīti ettha pana maggapaññāva adhippetā.

The term 'pertaining to the fundamentals of the noble practice' (ādibrahmacariyikā): this is a designation for the four great virtues that are the beginning of the noble practice of the path. ‘In every way’ (sabbaso): in all respects. ‘The dhammas’ (dhammā): the dhammas of the four truths. ‘They are thoroughly inspected with wisdom’: they are well seen by the wisdom of the path together with insight. ‘They have been touched by liberation’: they are touched by the liberation that is the fruit of arahantship through the touch of knowledge. ‘Mindfulness is well established internally’: mindfulness is well established right within oneself. ‘I will support with wisdom’: I will support with the wisdom of insight. ‘I will thoroughly inspect with wisdom’: here too, the wisdom of insight is intended. But in the phrase ‘or I will support the dhamma that has been touched in each case with wisdom,’ it is the wisdom of the path that is intended.

4. Seyyāsuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Discourse on Postures

246. Catutthe petāti kālakatā vuccanti. Uttānā sentīti te yebhuyyena uttānakāva sayanti. Atha vā pettivisaye nibbattā petā nāma, te appamaṃsalohitattā aṭṭhisaṅghātajaṭitā ekena passena sayituṃ na sakkonti, uttānāva senti. Anattamano hotīti tejussadattā sīho migarājā dve purimapāde ekasmiṃ, pacchimapāde ekasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhapetvā naṅguṭṭhaṃ antarasatthimhi pakkhipitvā purimapādapacchimapādanaṅguṭṭhānaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ sallakkhetvā dvinnaṃ purimapādānaṃ matthake sīsaṃ ṭhapetvā sayati. Divasampi sayitvā pabujjhamāno na uttasanto pabujjhati, sīsaṃ pana ukkhipitvā purimapādādīnaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ sallakkhetvā sace kiñci ṭhānaṃ [V 2.0393] vijahitvā ṭhitaṃ hoti, “nayidaṃ tuyhaṃ jātiyā, na sūrabhāvassa anurūpa”nti anattamano hutvā tattheva sayati, na gocarāya pakkamati. Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – “anattamano hotī”ti. Avijahitvā ṭhite pana “tuyhaṃ jātiyā ca sūrabhāvassa ca anurūpamida”nti haṭṭhatuṭṭho uṭṭhāya sīhavijambhanaṃ vijambhitvā kesarabhāraṃ vidhunitvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ [P 3.0219] naditvā gocarāya pakkamati. Tena vuttaṃ – “attamano hotī”ti.

246. In the fourth sutta, those who have passed away are called 'peta'. As for 'they lie on their backs', they mostly lie on their backs. Alternatively, those reborn in the peta-realm are called 'peta'; because they have little flesh and blood and are entangled with a collection of bones, they cannot lie on one side and so lie on their backs. As for 'he becomes displeased': The lion, the king of beasts, because of his great majesty, places his two front paws in one spot and his hind paws in one spot, tucking his tail between his thighs. Having marked the place where his front paws, hind paws, and tail rest, he lies down, placing his head on his two front paws. Even after sleeping for a day, upon waking, he does not wake up startled. But lifting his head, he observes the positions of his front paws and so on. If any part has shifted from its place, thinking, 'This is not befitting your birth, nor your heroic nature,' he becomes displeased, lies down right there, and does not go out to his feeding ground. It is with reference to this that it was said, 'he becomes displeased.' But if they have not shifted, thinking, 'This is befitting your birth and your heroic nature,' he becomes delighted and satisfied, rises, stretches a lion's stretch, shakes out his mane, roars a lion's roar three times, and goes out to his feeding ground. For this reason it was said, 'he becomes pleased.'

5. Thūpārahasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Thūpāraha Sutta

247. Pañcame rājā cakkavattīti ettha kasmā bhagavā agāramajjhe vasitvā kālakatassa rañño thūpakaraṇaṃ anujānāti, na sīlavato puthujjanabhikkhussāti? Anacchariyattā. Puthujjanabhikkhūnañhi thūpe anuññāyamāne tambapaṇṇidīpe tāva thūpānaṃ okāso na bhaveyya, tathā aññesu ṭhānesu. Tasmā “anacchariyā te bhavissantī”ti nānujānāti. Cakkavattī rājā ekova nibbattati, tenassa thūpo acchariyo hoti. Puthujjanasīlavato pana parinibbutabhikkhuno viya mahantampi sakkāraṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Chaṭṭhasattamāni uttānatthāneva.

247. In the fifth sutta, regarding 'a wheel-turning monarch': Why does the Blessed One permit the making of a stupa for a king who has died having lived in the household life, but not for a virtuous worldling-monk? Because of it not being extraordinary. Indeed, if stupas for worldling-monks were permitted, to begin with, there would not be enough space for stupas on the island of Tambapaṇṇi, and likewise in other places. Therefore, he does not permit it, thinking, 'They would not be extraordinary.' A wheel-turning monarch arises only one at a time; for that reason, his stupa is extraordinary. However, for a virtuous worldling-monk, it is indeed fitting to pay great honor, just as for a monk who has attained Parinibbāna. The sixth and seventh suttas are indeed clear in meaning.

8. Paṭhamavohārasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the First Vohāra Sutta

250. Aṭṭhame [M 2.0396] anariyavohārāti anariyānaṃ kathā. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

250. In the eighth sutta, anariyavohārā means the talk of the ignoble. In the remaining suttas also, this is the method.

Āpattibhayavaggo pañcamo.

The Chapter on the Fear of Offenses is the fifth.

Pañcamapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fifth Fifty is finished.

(26) 6. Abhiññāvaggo

(26) 6. The Chapter on Direct Knowledge

1-3. Abhiññāsuttādivaṇṇanā

1-3. Commentary on the Abhiññā Sutta and Others

254-256. Chaṭṭhassa [V 2.0394] paṭhame abhiññāyāti jānitvā. Samatho ca vipassanā cāti cittekaggatā ca saṅkhārapariggahavipassanāñāṇañca. Vijjā ca vimutti cāti maggañāṇavijjā ca sesā sampayuttakadhammā ca. Dutiye [P 3.0220] anariyapariyesanāti anariyānaṃ esanā gavesanā. Jarādhammanti jarāsabhāvaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Tatiyaṃ uttānameva.

254-256. In the first sutta of the sixth chapter, abhiññāya means having known. Samatho ca vipassanā ca means one-pointedness of mind and the knowledge of insight that comprehends formations. Vijjā ca vimutti ca means the knowledge that is path-knowledge and the remaining associated states. In the second sutta, anariyapariyesanā means the seeking and searching of the ignoble. Jarādhammaṃ means having the nature of aging. In the remaining terms also, this is the method. The third sutta is self-evident indeed.

4. Mālukyaputtasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Mālukyaputta Sutta

257. Catutthe mālukyaputtoti mālukyabrāhmaṇiyā putto. Etthāti etasmiṃ tava ovādayācane. Iminā theraṃ apasādetipi ussādetipi. Kathaṃ? Ayaṃ kira daharakāle paccayesu laggo hutvā pacchā mahallakakāle araññavāsaṃ patthento kammaṭṭhānaṃ yācati. Atha bhagavā “ettha dahare kiṃ vakkhāma, mālukyaputto viya tumhepi taruṇakāle paccayesu laggitvā mahallakakāle araññaṃ pavisitvā samaṇadhammaṃ kareyyāthā”ti iminā adhippāyena bhaṇanto theraṃ apasādeti nāma. Yasmā pana thero mahallakakāleva araññaṃ pavisitvā samaṇadhammaṃ kātukāmo, tasmā bhagavā “ettha dahare kiṃ vakkhāma, ayaṃ amhākaṃ mālukyaputto mahallakakālepi araññaṃ pavisitvā samaṇadhammaṃ kātukāmo [M 2.0397] kammaṭṭhānaṃ yācati. Tumhe tāva taruṇakālepi vīriyaṃ na karothā”ti iminā adhippāyena bhaṇanto theraṃ ussādeti nāmāti yojanā.

257. In the fourth sutta, 'Mālukyaputta' is the son of the brahmin lady Mālukyā. 'Ettha' means 'in this request of yours for an exhortation.' With this, He both disparages and encourages the elder. How so? It is said that this elder, in his youth, having been attached to the requisites, later in his old age, desiring to dwell in the forest, asks for a meditation subject. Then the Blessed One, speaking with the intention of disparaging the elder, is said to have spoken thus: 'Here, what shall we say to the young monks? Like Mālukyaputta, you too, having become attached to requisites in your youth, might enter the forest in old age to practice the ascetic's duties.' On the other hand, because the elder, even in old age, was desirous of entering the forest and practicing the ascetic's duties, the Blessed One, speaking with the intention of encouraging the elder, is said to have spoken thus: 'Here, what shall we say to the young monks? This Mālukyaputta of ours, even in old age, being desirous of entering the forest to practice the ascetic's duties, asks for a meditation subject. You, on the other hand, should make an effort even in your youth.' This is the construction.

5-10. Kulasuttādivaṇṇanā

5-10. Commentary on the Kula Sutta and Others

258-263. Pañcame [V 2.0395][P 3.0221] ādhipacce ṭhapentīti bhaṇḍāgārikaṭṭhāne ṭhapenti. Chaṭṭhe vaṇṇasampannoti sarīravaṇṇena samannāgato. Balasampannoti kāyabalena samannāgato. Bhikkhuvāre vaṇṇasampannoti guṇavaṇṇena samannāgato. Balasampannoti vīriyabalena samannāgato. Javasampannoti ñāṇajavena samannāgato. Sattamepi eseva nayo. Sesamettha uttānamevāti.

258-263. In the fifth sutta, 'they establish in authority' means they establish in the position of treasurer. In the sixth sutta, 'endowed with beauty' means endowed with physical complexion. 'Endowed with strength' means endowed with bodily strength. In the section on the bhikkhu, 'endowed with beauty' means endowed with the beauty of virtue; 'endowed with strength' means endowed with the strength of energy; 'endowed with swiftness' means endowed with the swiftness of knowledge. In the seventh sutta also, this is the method. The rest here is self-evident.

Abhiññāvaggo chaṭṭho.

The Chapter on Direct Knowledge, the Sixth.

(27) 7. Kammapathavaggavaṇṇanā

(27) 7. Commentary on the Kammapatha Vagga

264-273. Kammapathavaggepi [V 2.0396] dasapi kammapathā lokiyalokuttaramissakāva kathitā.

264-273. In the Kammapatha Vagga also, the ten courses of action are taught as a mixture of the worldly and the supramundane.

(28) 8. Rāgapeyyālavaṇṇanā

(28) 8. Commentary on the Repetition Series on Lust

274-783. Rāgapeyyālaṃ arahattaṃ pāpetvā kathitaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

The Repetition Series on Lust was taught, culminating in arahantship. The rest is self-evident in all respects.

Manorathapūraṇiyā aṅguttaranikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

In the Manorathapūraṇī, the Commentary on the Aṅguttara Nikāya,

Catukkanipātassa saṃvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Book of the Fours is finished.
